# Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center



## The Needs Of The Patient Come First


Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is LA’s premier state-of-the-art oral and maxillofacial surgery practice located in one of LA’s most iconic neighborhoods. We are proud to provide personalized full-scope oral and maxillofacial surgery for patients utilizing today’s most modern surgical diagnostic and treatment technologies.

Our board-certified surgeons and staff have extensive training and experience in surgical procedures including dental implants, wisdom teeth removal, IV sedation and general anesthesia, impacted teeth, facial/dental trauma, “teeth in a day” surgery, and many other contemporary oral surgery & implant services. We focus on the needs of each patient to provide a comfortable experience in a relaxing and modern environment in our West Los Angeles office.

What To Expect


### Patient Registration


Save time during your visit by downloading and filling out our patient registration form. Patients who have registered online may arrive 5 to 10 minutes before their scheduled appointment. Patients who have not, should arrive no less than 20 minutes early to complete the patient paperwork in office.


### Insurance


We work hand-in-hand to maximize your insurance benefits. We make every effort to provide you with the finest care and the most convenient financial options and will call your insurance, on your behalf, to calculate the most accurate estimate. We are participating providers for most insurance companies and work hand-in-hand with you to maximize your insurance reimbursement for covered procedures.


### Length Of Procedure


The length of your procedure will depend on the procedure taking place. Wisdom teeth procedures typically take 30 to 60 minutes. Single tooth extractions usually take 20-30 minutes. Implant and bone grafting procedures can vary. You can expect to be in our office 1.5 to 2 hours which accounts for initial paperwork, consultation, procedure, and in-office recovery time.

# Accessibility Statement


We are continuously working to improve the accessibility of content on our website. Below, you’ll find a few recommendations to help make your browsing experience more accessible.

If you have trouble seeing web pages, the US Social Security Administration offers these tips for optimizing your computer and browser to improve your online experience:

Use your computer to read web pages out loud

Use the keyboard to navigate screens

Increase text size

Magnify your screen

Change background and text colors

Make your mouse pointer more visible (Windows only)

If you are looking for alternatives to your mouse and keyboard, speech recognition software such as Dragon Naturally Speaking may help you navigate web pages and online services. This software allows the user to move focus around a web page or application screen through voice controls.

If you are deaf or hard of hearing, there are several accessibility features available to you.


## Closed Captioning


Closed captioning provides a transcript for the audio track of a video presentation that is synchronized with the video and audio tracks. Captions are generally visually displayed over the video, which benefits people who are deaf or hard of hearing as well as anyone who cannot hear the audio due to noisy environments. Most of our video content includes captions, which you can learn how to turn on and off by visiting YouTube.


## Volume Controls


Your computer, tablet, or mobile device has built-in volume control features. Each video and audio service has its own additional volume controls. Try adjusting both your device’s and your media player’s volume controls to optimize your listening experience.

​​​​​​​If the recommendations above do not meet your needs, we invite you to contact us at for assistance.

# Before Anesthesia



## Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon



### At Home


Do not eat or drink anything for at least 6 hours before your IV sedation/general anesthesia procedure (for morning surgery that means nothing past midnight). Failure to follow this instruction may be life-threatening! If you need to take medications you can with a just small sip of water. Use the restroom prior to your appointment.

Do not ignore a head or a chest cold when oral surgery is to be performed. Call immediately if any symptoms are present; a change of appointment may be necessary.

Please arrive wearing a loose short-sleeved shirt.

Do not wear fingernail polish or acrylic fingernails.

Make arrangements for someone to stay with you at the office, throughout your procedure, and drive you home after.They will not be able to leave during your procedure. Uber, Lyft, and taxis are not appropriate rides home.

If you normally wear contacts, we ask you to wear your glasses on the day of the procedure.

Have someone at home to take care of/watch you for the remainder of the day after surgery.

Do not drive or make important decisions within 24 hours after surgery.


### At The Office


Patients 18 years or younger will need a parent/legal guardian present to sign a medical history and consent forms.

Please bring all dental and medical insurance cards with you to the office.

Please bring you referral card from your dentist or specialist.

If your dentist or physician has taken x-rays, you may forward them or bring them to our office. If additional films are necessary, they can be taken at our office. Before your procedure, a dental assistant will go over your medical history. Your doctor will also visit you to answer any questions and go over concerns you may have.

# Oral Surgery Pre-Operative Instructions


The preparation of your mouth before the placement of a denture (or prosthesis) is referred to as pre-prosthetic surgery. Some patients require minor oral surgical procedures before receiving a partial or complete denture, in order to ensure the maximum level of comfort and stability.

Since a dental prosthetic sits atop the bone ridge, that surface needs to be smooth. It must be of the proper shape and size. Pre-prosthetic surgery can be employed to mold the bone into the proper shape. Such procedures can include:

Torus/Tori removal

Tuberosity reduction

Alveoplasty

Removal of excess gum tissue

​​​​​​​Pre-prosthetic surgery procedures are accomplished in complete comfort at our office. Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi will discuss surgical and anesthetic options with you during your consultation appointment.

# Post-Operative Instructions



## ***Please Read All of These Instructions Carefully***


Sometimes the after-effects of oral surgery are quite minimal, so not all of the instructions may apply. Common sense will often dictate what you should do. However, if you have a question, follow these guidelines or call our office to reach the doctor on call for clarification.24-hour contact: 310-954-9449.


### DAY OF SURGERY


FIRST HOUR: Bite down gently but firmly on the gauze packs that have been placed over the surgical areas, making sure they remain in place. Do not change them for the first hour unless the bleeding is not controlled. The packs may be gently removed after one hour. If active bleeding persists, place enough new gauze to obtain pressure over the surgical site for another hour. The gauze may then be changed as necessary (typically every 45 – 60 minutes). It is best to moisten the gauze with tap water. Once the active bleeding has stopped then remove the gauze altogether and expect light and intermittent oozing of blood for the next 12-24 hours.

WOUND CARE: Do not disturb the surgical area today. Do NOT rinse vigorously or probe the area with any objects. You may brush your teeth gently, preferably starting tomorrow morning but avoiding the surgical area(s). PLEASE DO NOT SMOKE for at least 72 hours, since this is very detrimental to healing and may cause a dry socket.

OOZING: Intermittent bleeding or oozing overnight is normal. Bleeding may be controlled by placing fresh gauze over the areas and biting on the gauze for 45 – 60 minutes at a time.

PERSISTENT BLEEDING: Bleeding should never be severe. If so, it usually means that the packs are being clenched between teeth only and are not exerting pressure on the surgical areas. Try repositioning the packs. If bleeding persists or becomes heavy, you may use a black tea bag (moistened with warm water) placed on the surgical area with firm biting pressure for 45–60 minutes. If bleeding remains uncontrolled, please call our office.

SWELLING: Swelling is often associated with oral surgery. It can be minimized by using a cold pack, ice bag, or a bag of frozen vegetables (such as peas) wrapped in a towel and applied firmly to the cheek adjacent to the surgical area. This should be applied 20 minutes on and twenty minutes off during the first 24 hours after surgery. If you have been prescribed medicine for the control of swelling, be sure to take it as directed.

PAIN: Unfortunately most oral surgery is accompanied by some degree of discomfort. You will usually have a prescription for pain medication. If you take the first pill before the anesthetic has worn off, you should be able to manage any discomfort better. Some patients find that stronger pain medicine causes nausea, but if you precede each pain pill with a small amount of food, it will reduce the chance that nausea will occur. The effects of pain medications vary widely among individuals. Remember that the most severe pain is usually within the first 12-24 hours after the local anesthetic wears off; after that, your need for medicine should lessen. If you find you are taking large amounts of pain medicine at frequent intervals, please call our office If you anticipate needing more prescription medication for the weekend, you must call for a refill during weekday business hours.

NAUSEA: Nausea is not uncommon after surgery. Sometimes pain medications are the cause. Nausea can be reduced by preceding each pain pill with a small amount of soft food and taking the pill with a large volume of water. Try to keep taking clear fluids and minimize the dosing of pain medications, but call us if you do not feel better. Classic Coca-Cola or ginger may help with nausea.

DIET: Eat any nourishing food that can be eaten with comfort. Avoid extremely hot foods. Do not use a straw for the first 7 days after surgery. It is sometimes advisable, but not absolutely required, to confine the first day’s intake to liquids or pureed foods (soups, puddings, yogurt, milkshakes, etc.). It is best to avoid foods like nuts, sunflower seeds, chips, taco shells, popcorn, etc., which may get lodged in the socket areas. Over the next several days you may gradually progress to solid foods. It is important not to skip meals! If you take nourishment regularly you will feel better, gain strength, have less discomfort, and heal faster. If you are a diabetic, maintain your normal eating habits or follow instructions given by your doctor.

SHARP EDGES: If you feel something hard or sharp edges in the surgical areas, you are likely feeling the bony walls, which once supported the extracted teeth. Occasionally, small slivers of bone may work themselves out during the following week or so. If they cause concern or discomfort, please call our office.


### INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE SECOND AND THIRD DAYS


MOUTH RINSES: Keeping your mouth clean after surgery is essential. Use a teaspoon of salt dissolved in an 8-ounce glass of warm water and gently rinse with portions of the solution, taking five minutes to use the entire glassful. Repeat as often as you like, but at least two or three times daily.

BRUSHING: Begin your normal oral hygiene routine as soon as possible after surgery. Soreness and swelling may not permit vigorous brushing, but please make every effort to clean your teeth within the bounds of comfort.

HOT APPLICATIONS: You may apply warm compresses to the skin over the areas of swelling (hot water bottle, hot moist towels, heating pad) for 20 minutes on and 20 minutes off to help soothe tender areas. This will also help decrease swelling and stiffness.

HEALING: Normal healing after tooth extraction should be as follows: The first two days after surgery are generally the most uncomfortable and there is usually some swelling. On the third day you should be more comfortable and, although still swollen, can usually begin a more substantial diet. The remainder of the post-operative course should be a gradual, steady improvement. If you don’t see continued improvement, please call our office. If you are given a plastic irrigating syringe, DO NOT use it for the first five days. Then use it daily according to the instructions until you are certain the tooth socket has closed completely and that there is no chance of any food particles lodging in the socket.

It is our desire that your recovery be as smooth and pleasant as possible. Following these instructions will assist you, but if you have questions about your progress, please call our office. Calling during office hours will afford a faster response to your question or concern.

PLEASE NOTE: Telephone calls for narcotic (pain killer) prescription renewal are ONLY accepted during office hours as these cannot be called into the pharmacy any longer.

# TMJ Disorders (TMD)


TMJ disorders can make everyday actions like eating, speaking, or simply opening your mouth surprisingly painful. The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) connects your lower jaw to your skull, and when this joint is disrupted, it can trigger jaw pain, clicking sounds, and persistent headaches. For many patients in West Los Angeles, these symptoms go unaddressed for years, allowing the condition to progress and compound over time.

At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, our board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons, Dr. Saman Vahedi and Dr. Jonathan Shadi, provide personalized TMJ evaluation and treatment using today’s most advanced diagnostic technologies. From our West LA office on Wilshire Boulevard, we work with patients across a wide range of TMJ presentations, from mild discomfort to complex cases requiring surgical intervention. Learn more about the full range of services we offer on our Procedures page.


## What Is the Temporomandibular Joint?


The temporomandibular joint acts as a hinge on each side of your face, connecting your jawbone to your skull and making it possible to open and close your mouth, chew, speak, and swallow. The joint is supported by a network of muscles, ligaments, and a small disc that cushions movement between the bones. When any part of this system is stressed, injured, or misaligned, a TMJ disorder (also referred to as TMD) can develop.

UCSF Health notes that TMJ disorders affect over 10 million people in the United States and that certain factors, including arthritis, injury, and teeth grinding, can disrupt the joint’s normal function. Because the joint operates on both sides of the face simultaneously, even minor dysfunction can have a significant impact on daily comfort and quality of life.


## Common Symptoms of TMJ Disorders


TMJ disorders can present differently from patient to patient, which is part of why they are often difficult to identify without a thorough evaluation. Jaw pain or tenderness on one or both sides of the face is among the most frequently reported symptoms. Many patients also notice a clicking, popping, or grating sensation when opening or closing the mouth, along with headaches or pain that radiates into the neck or ears. Difficulty chewing, locking of the jaw in an open or closed position, and nighttime teeth clenching or grinding (bruxism) are all recognized signs of a TMJ disorder.

Jaw Pain or Tenderness

Soreness on one or both sides of the face, often near the joint, temple, or ear.

Clicking or Popping Sounds

Audible or felt clicking, grating, or popping when opening or closing the jaw.

Headaches and Ear Pain

Chronic headaches, neck aches, or ear discomfort not linked to infection or sinus issues.

Difficulty Chewing

Pain or discomfort when biting, or a noticeable change in how your upper and lower teeth come together.

Jaw Locking

Difficulty fully opening or closing the mouth, or a jaw that catches or locks in position.

Teeth Grinding (Bruxism)

Clenching or grinding during sleep that leads to tooth wear, sensitivity, or morning jaw fatigue.

Some patients also develop tooth sensitivity or notice worn-down tooth surfaces as bruxism continues over time. If you experience any combination of these symptoms consistently, scheduling an evaluation early may prevent further joint damage and reduce long-term treatment complexity.


## What Causes TMJ Disorders?


TMJ disorders develop for a variety of reasons, and identifying the contributing factors is important for creating an effective treatment plan. Common causes include traumatic injury to the jaw or surrounding area, chronic teeth clenching and grinding (bruxism), arthritis affecting the joint itself, and displacement of the disc between the jawbone and socket. Poor posture, particularly when sustained over long periods, can also place undue strain on the jaw muscles and contribute to TMD symptoms over time. Stress is another frequently overlooked contributor, as tension in the jaw muscles often increases during periods of high stress.


## How TMJ Disorders Are Diagnosed


Accurately diagnosing TMJ disorders requires the kind of thorough evaluation that goes beyond a standard dental exam. Our surgeons begin with a detailed review of your medical history and a physical assessment of your jaw joints, muscles, and bite function. In many cases, we use cone beam 3D imaging to get a precise view of the joint anatomy, identifying structural issues that may not appear on conventional X-rays. This technology is available directly in our West Los Angeles office, allowing for faster and more targeted diagnosis without outside referrals.


## Treatment Options for TMJ Disorders


Treatment for TMJ disorders is tailored to the underlying cause and severity of each patient’s condition. Our approach moves from conservative to surgical only when necessary, and our goal is always to relieve pain and restore function in the least invasive way possible. Depending on your evaluation, treatment may include:

Oral appliances such as custom night guards or occlusal splints to reduce clenching and grinding during sleep

Physical therapy and targeted jaw exercises to improve mobility and reduce muscle tension

Anti-inflammatory medications or muscle relaxers for short-term relief of acute symptoms

Dietary modifications and jaw rest techniques, such as avoiding hard or chewy foods during flare-ups

Arthrocentesis or TMJ arthroscopy, minimally invasive procedures used to flush or repair the joint

Open joint surgery for complex structural damage when conservative measures have not provided lasting relief

Not every patient requires surgery. Many cases respond well to conservative care, and we take care to match each patient with the most appropriate level of treatment for their specific presentation.


## Why Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons Treat TMJ


Oral and maxillofacial surgeons are uniquely positioned to treat the full spectrum of TMJ disorders, from conservative appliance therapy through arthroscopic and open joint procedures. This breadth of surgical training allows our team to address both the mild and the structurally complex cases of TMD, rather than being limited to non-surgical options. For patients whose TMJ symptoms are connected to a broader jaw alignment concern, orthognathic (corrective jaw) surgery may also be worth exploring as part of a longer-term treatment plan.

Living with Jaw Pain in Los Angeles?

Dr. Vahedi and Dr. Shadi offer board-certified TMJ evaluation and treatment at our West Los Angeles office. Same-day consultations are available.

Request an Appointment


## What to Do If You Have TMJ Symptoms


If you have been experiencing persistent jaw pain, clicking, or headaches, the most important step is to schedule a consultation with an oral and maxillofacial surgeon for a proper evaluation. In the meantime, you can reduce stress on the joint by keeping your teeth slightly apart when not eating or speaking, avoiding hard and chewy foods, and applying a warm compress to sore jaw muscles. Habits like nail-biting, daytime clenching, or resting your chin on your hand can place additional pressure on the joint and may worsen symptoms over time. If nighttime grinding is a concern, our team can evaluate you for a custom night guard as part of your initial consultation.


## TMJ Disorder Care at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, Dr. Vahedi and Dr. Shadi bring board-certified training in oral and maxillofacial surgery to every TMJ evaluation. Dr. Vahedi is double board-certified in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Medicine and is fellowship trained in complex reconstructive surgery, with over 15 years of experience serving West LA patients. Our office offers same-day consultations, IV sedation and general anesthesia for surgical TMJ procedures, and advanced cone beam 3D imaging for precise diagnosis. We accept most major PPO insurance plans, and our bilingual team provides care in English, Spanish, and Farsi.

If you have been living with jaw pain, clicking sounds, or chronic headaches in the Los Angeles area, you do not have to continue without answers. Contact us to request an appointment and let us help you find lasting relief.


## Frequently Asked Questions About TMJ Disorders in Los Angeles



### How do I know if my jaw pain requires a professional evaluation?+


Occasional jaw soreness can stem from temporary stress or muscle tension, but certain signs suggest the joint itself may be involved and warrant evaluation by an oral and maxillofacial surgeon. If you are experiencing clicking or popping when you open your mouth, pain that radiates into your ear or temples, difficulty fully opening or closing your jaw, or symptoms that have persisted for more than a few weeks, we recommend scheduling a consultation. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center in Los Angeles, our team can determine whether your symptoms are consistent with a TMJ disorder and advise on the appropriate level of care.


### What happens during a TMJ evaluation at Wilshire Oral Surgery?+


During your initial visit at our West Los Angeles office, Dr. Vahedi or Dr. Shadi will review your medical and dental history, assess your jaw range of motion, and evaluate your muscles and joints for tenderness or dysfunction. In many cases, we use cone beam 3D imaging to examine the joint anatomy in detail, identifying disc displacement, bone changes, or structural issues not visible on standard X-rays. Based on this evaluation, we develop a treatment plan tailored to your specific presentation and goals.


### Will I need surgery for my TMJ disorder?+


Most patients with TMJ disorders respond well to conservative care and do not require surgery. Our approach always begins with the least invasive options, including custom night guards, physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medications, and dietary modifications. Surgery becomes a consideration only when conservative treatments have been thoroughly tried without meaningful improvement, or when imaging reveals significant structural joint damage. When surgical treatment is appropriate, our board-certified surgeons offer arthrocentesis, arthroscopy, and open joint surgery depending on the nature and severity of the condition.


### What can I do at home to reduce TMJ symptoms?+


A few practical habits can meaningfully reduce strain on the temporomandibular joint between appointments. Keeping your teeth slightly apart when you are not eating or speaking avoids the low-level clenching many people carry without realizing it, and eating softer foods during flare-ups reduces mechanical stress on the joint. Applying a warm compress to sore jaw muscles and avoiding habits like nail-biting, gum chewing, or resting your chin on your hand can also help. If you grind your teeth at night, a custom night guard from our Los Angeles office may provide significant relief by cushioning the joint during sleep.


### Does insurance cover TMJ treatment?+


Coverage for TMJ treatment varies depending on your insurance plan. Some PPO plans cover diagnostic evaluations and certain conservative treatments such as custom oral appliances when TMJ is documented as a medical diagnosis, and surgical procedures may be covered under the medical portion of your policy rather than the dental benefit. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we work with most major PPO insurance plans and can help verify your specific coverage and outline all associated costs during your consultation.


### Why should I see an oral and maxillofacial surgeon for TMJ disorders?+


Oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete additional hospital-based surgical residency training beyond dental school, equipping them to manage TMJ disorders across the full treatment spectrum, from conservative appliance therapy to arthroscopic and open joint procedures. Many other providers are limited to non-surgical options only. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center in Los Angeles, our surgeons also have access to advanced in-office cone beam 3D imaging, enabling more precise diagnosis than a standard clinical exam can provide on its own.

# ​​​​​​​IV Sedation/General Anesthesia


Dental anxiety is one of the most common reasons people delay the oral surgery care they need. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we believe that fear should never stand between you and a healthy, pain-free mouth. Our team offers four levels of sedation and anesthesia so every patient, regardless of anxiety level or procedure complexity, can receive care in complete comfort.

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi completed their oral and maxillofacial surgery residencies at top academic medical centers, where their training included a dedicated 4 to 6 month anesthesia rotation working directly alongside anesthesiologists and nurse-anesthetists. That hands-on hospital training, combined with over three years of in-residency IV sedation experience across oral surgery and multiple other surgical specialties, means you are in the care of surgeons who administer anesthesia with the same rigor as a hospital operating room.

15+ Years

Anesthesia Experience

4 Levels

Sedation Available

West LA

Prime Location

Board Certified

Oral Surgeons


## Our Four Sedation and Anesthesia Options


Every patient is different, and no single approach fits everyone. During your consultation, our surgeons review your medical history, the nature of your procedure, your anxiety level, and your personal preferences before recommending the right option for you. The American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons recognizes oral and maxillofacial surgeons as the specialty most extensively trained to administer all levels of anesthesia safely in an office setting.

Nitrous Oxide — Inhaled through a mask for mild relaxation. You remain fully conscious and can drive home right after. Best for shorter procedures or light anxiety.

Oral Conscious Sedation — A prescribed pill taken before your appointment. You feel deeply relaxed and often have little memory of the procedure. Requires a driver.

IV Sedation — Delivered through an IV for a sleep-like state with real-time depth adjustment. Most common for wisdom teeth and implants. Requires a driver.

General Anesthesia — Full unconsciousness for complex cases or severe anxiety. Administered by hospital-trained surgeons using OR-level monitoring protocols.


## Who Is a Good Candidate for Sedation


You may benefit from sedation or anesthesia if you experience any of the following:

Dental Anxiety or Phobia

Moderate to severe anxiety that makes it difficult to get through appointments.

Strong Gag Reflex

A sensitive gag reflex that triggers during treatment and makes work difficult.

Sensory Sensitivity

Heightened sensitivity to dental sounds, smells, or the physical sensations of treatment.

Complex Procedure

A lengthy or multi-step surgery where comfort over an extended period is essential.

Past Trauma

A history of difficult or traumatic dental experiences that create anticipatory fear.

Difficulty Getting Numb

Local anesthesia alone doesn’t provide adequate comfort during procedures.

Not all sedation levels are appropriate for every patient or every procedure. Our surgeons will review your full medical history, current medications, allergies, and surgical history during a thorough pre-operative assessment before making any recommendation.

Ready for a Comfortable, Anxiety-Free Visit?

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi are here to help you choose the right sedation option and make your procedure as comfortable as possible.

Request an Appointment

or call (310) 954-9449


## What to Expect Before, During, and After Sedation


Preparation and recovery vary depending on which sedation level you choose. Here is how the process works:

Consultation

We review your medical history, medications, and anxiety level, then recommend the right sedation option for your procedure.

Day-of Prep

Fast for 8 hours (IV or general), arrange a driver, wear comfortable clothing, and skip contact lenses or nail polish on surgery day.

During Surgery

Our team continuously monitors your oxygen, blood pressure, heart rate, and airway. You are never left unattended under sedation.

Recovery

Nitrous wears off in minutes. For oral, IV, or general sedation, rest in our recovery area until stable, then your escort drives you home.

For complete preparation details, review our before anesthesia instructions and pre-operative instructions.


## IV Sedation vs. General Anesthesia


Patients often ask how IV sedation and general anesthesia differ. Here is a side-by-side comparison to help clarify the key distinctions:

IV Sedation

General Anesthesia

Level of consciousness

## A Note on Provider Training and Safety


Not all sedation providers have the same level of training. Some dental offices offer IV sedation after a short continuing education course lasting only a weekend or a few days. Our surgeons, by contrast, completed full hospital residencies that included a mandatory rotation on the anesthesiology service, where they functioned as anesthesia residents under the direct supervision of attending anesthesiologists. We encourage every patient to ask their provider about their training background before accepting any sedation.


## Meet Your West LA Oral Surgery Team


Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi, DDS

Board Certified Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon

Dr. Shadi earned his B.S. in Neuroscience from UCLA and his dental degree from the USC School of Dentistry, where he was named to the Dean’s List multiple times. He completed his residency in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery at UCSF-Fresno, with training that included an extensive anesthesia rotation. He is well versed in IV general anesthesia and all aspects of oral and maxillofacial surgery.

Dr. Saman Vahedi, DDS, MD

Diplomate, American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons

Dr. Vahedi earned his undergraduate degree from UCLA and his DDS from the Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry at USC. He completed his medical training and residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, serving as Chief Resident from 2013 to 2014. He has extensive experience in IV general anesthesia, complex implant surgery, bone grafting, and all aspects of oral and maxillofacial surgery.


## Frequently Asked Questions About Sedation and Anesthesia


Will I be completely unconscious under IV sedation?

Not necessarily. IV sedation places you in a deeply relaxed, sleep-like state where most patients have little or no memory of the procedure, but it is not the same as full general anesthesia. You may be able to respond to verbal cues if needed. The depth of sedation can be adjusted in real time by our surgeons based on how your body responds during the procedure.

How do I know which sedation option is right for me?

The right sedation level depends on your anxiety level, your medical history, the complexity of your procedure, and your personal preferences. During your consultation, our surgeons will walk through each option with you and make a recommendation based on your individual situation. We never pressure patients into a particular level of sedation, and your comfort and safety always come first.

Can I eat or drink before my sedation appointment?

For IV sedation and general anesthesia, you must fast for at least eight hours before your procedure, including no food, water, gum, or mints. For nitrous oxide or oral sedation, your surgeon will give you specific instructions at your consultation, as guidelines can vary based on your individual circumstances.

Is sedation safe for anxious patients?

Yes. When administered by properly trained oral and maxillofacial surgeons in an appropriately equipped office, sedation is very safe and well-tolerated by the vast majority of patients. Our team uses continuous monitoring of your vital signs throughout every procedure. If you have a significant medical history, we may request medical clearance from your physician before proceeding.

Will I need someone to drive me home?

Yes, for oral sedation, IV sedation, and general anesthesia, you must have a responsible adult with you who can drive you home and stay with you for the rest of the day. We will not be able to perform the procedure if you arrive without an escort. For nitrous oxide only, most patients can drive themselves home once the effects have fully resolved.

What is the difference between IV sedation and general anesthesia?

IV sedation produces a deep, sleep-like relaxation where you may still respond to verbal prompts, while general anesthesia renders you completely unconscious and unaware. General anesthesia involves higher medication levels and more intensive monitoring and is typically reserved for more complex procedures or patients with particular medical or psychological needs. Your surgeon will discuss which is appropriate during your consultation.


## Schedule Your Sedation Consultation in Los Angeles


There is no reason to let anxiety keep you from the oral surgery care you need. Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi serve patients throughout the Los Angeles area, from West Hollywood to Santa Monica to Beverly Hills. We are located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd, Suite 326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. Call or text us at (310) 954-9449, or request an appointment online to get started today.

# Pre-Prosthetic Surgery Instructions


The preparation of your mouth before the placement of a denture (or prosthesis) is referred to as pre-prosthetic surgery. Some patients require minor oral surgical procedures before receiving a partial or complete denture, in order to ensure the maximum level of comfort and stability.

Since a dental prosthetic sits atop the bone ridge, that surface needs to be smooth. It must be of the proper shape and size. Pre-prosthetic surgery can be employed to mold the bone into the proper shape. Such procedures can include:

Torus/Tori removal

Tuberosity reduction

Alveoplasty

Removal of excess gum tissue

​​​​​​​Pre-prosthetic surgery procedures are accomplished in complete comfort at our office. Dr Shadi and Dr. vahedi will discuss surgical and anesthetic options with you during your consultation appointment.

# About Us



## About Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


Choosing an oral surgeon is one of the more consequential healthcare decisions you can make. Whether you need a wisdom tooth removed, a dental implant placed, or a more complex surgical procedure, the training, technology, and environment your surgeon provides will shape every part of that experience. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, our surgeons and staff have built a practice in West Los Angeles that meets that standard at every level: board-level credentials, advanced in-office technology, and the kind of personalized attention that makes a real difference when you are facing oral surgery.

We serve patients from across the Westside, including Beverly Hills, Santa Monica, Brentwood, Culver City, Westwood, and the surrounding communities. Our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025 offers a modern, comfortable surgical environment where you can receive the full scope of oral and maxillofacial care without being referred across town for imaging, anesthesia, or additional procedures.


## Our Surgeons


Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is led by two board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons. You can read their full biographies on our Meet Us page, but here is a brief overview of the training that backs every procedure we perform.

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi, DDS

Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon

B.S. Neuroscience, UCLA (College Honors)

DDS, USC School of Dentistry (Dean’s List)

John Ingle Research Award, 2009

OMFS Internship, Veterans’ Affairs Hospital, Long Beach

OMFS Residency, UCSF–Fresno, 2014

View Dr. Shadi’s Bio →

Dr. Saman Vahedi, DDS

B.S. Molecular, Cell & Developmental Biology, UCLA

DDS, Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry, USC

OMFS Residency, University of Nebraska Medical Center

Chief Resident, 2013–2014

Diplomate, American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons

View Dr. Vahedi’s Bio →

Board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete four to six years of hospital-based residency training after dental school, rotating through anesthesiology, general surgery, internal medicine, and other disciplines. The American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery requires candidates to pass written and oral examinations reviewed by a panel of peers before certification is granted. This level of training distinguishes oral and maxillofacial surgeons from general dental providers, particularly for cases that involve bone loss, anatomical complexity, sedation, or multiple procedures in a single visit.


## What We Offer


Our practice provides the full scope of oral and maxillofacial surgery under one roof, eliminating the need for multiple specialist referrals across the Westside. Our surgeons and staff are trained and equipped to handle:

Single implants, multiple implant cases, and full-arch restoration

Learn More →

Surgical extractions including impacted and complex cases

Ridge augmentation and bone volume restoration for implant readiness

IV Sedation & Anesthesia

Administered in-office by our board-certified surgeons

On-site for same-visit surgical planning, no outside referrals

Comprehensive rehabilitation and pre-prosthetic surgery

Orthognathic Surgery

Corrective jaw procedures for function and alignment

Surgical exposure and treatment of impacted teeth

Facial Trauma & Fractures

Emergency and reconstructive care for facial injuries

Oral Pathology & Biopsies

Evaluation and tissue biopsy for oral lesions and abnormalities

PRF & Growth Factors

Platelet-Rich Fibrin therapy to support healing and recovery

Every treatment plan is built around your specific anatomy, goals, and timeline. We take the time to walk you through your options, explain what each procedure involves, and answer your questions before any clinical decision is made.


## Our Technology and Facility


Our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326 in West Los Angeles is equipped with the diagnostic and surgical technology that modern oral surgery requires.

3D Cone Beam CT

On-site imaging for precise, same-visit surgical planning with no outside referrals or delays.

In-Office Anesthesia

IV sedation and general anesthesia administered by the same board-certified surgeons performing your procedure.

Modern Surgical Suite

A comfortable, purpose-built environment with hospital-level monitoring standards in a private West LA office.

Our Location →

IV sedation and general anesthesia are administered by Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi themselves, using the same monitoring standards applied in hospital operating rooms. Patients who prefer to be sedated for their procedure, or whose cases require it, can undergo treatment in the same familiar office environment without the cost and complexity of a hospital or ambulatory surgery center visit.


## Serving the West Los Angeles Community


Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center has been part of the West Los Angeles community since our founding. Patients come to us from Beverly Hills, Santa Monica, Brentwood, Westwood, Century City, Sawtelle, Mar Vista, Culver City, and the surrounding areas, drawn by the combination of board-certified surgical credentials, advanced technology, and individualized care that is difficult to find in a single practice.

Whether you were referred by your general dentist, found us while researching your options, or are returning for additional treatment, we are glad you are here. Our team is committed to making every visit informative, comfortable, and productive, so you leave with a clear understanding of your oral health and a path forward that makes sense for your situation. You can also read what our patients say on our reviews page.

Ready to Schedule Your Consultation?

Our board-certified surgeons at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center are here to answer your questions and build a plan that fits your needs.

Request an Appointment or call (310) 846-8978

If you are ready to discuss your oral surgery needs with a board-certified surgeon, we invite you to request an appointment online or reach us through our contact page. Our team is available to answer questions, explain your options, and help you take the next step with confidence. You can also review our patient resources, including pre-operative and post-operative instructions, before your visit.

# Oral Surgeon in Brentwood, LA


Home › Areas We Serve › Oral Surgeon in Brentwood, CA

Brentwood is one of the most sought-after neighborhoods on the Westside of Los Angeles, and its residents expect the same level of excellence from their healthcare providers. Whether you are dealing with an impacted wisdom tooth, exploring dental implants, or facing a more complex oral surgery need, Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is conveniently located minutes away at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326 in Los Angeles. From Brentwood, our office is a short drive east along Wilshire Boulevard, making it one of the most accessible oral surgery practices for residents of this community.

Our practice is led by two fellowship-trained, board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons. You can learn more about our team and what sets our surgeons apart.

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi, DDS

B.S. Neuroscience, UCLA · DDS, USC School of Dentistry · Dean’s List · John Ingle Research Award (2009) · OMFS Internship, Veterans’ Affairs Hospital

Dr. Saman Vahedi, DDS

## Oral Surgery Procedures We Offer Brentwood Patients


We offer a full range of oral and maxillofacial surgery services for Brentwood patients across all stages of life. Whether your need is preventive, restorative, or reconstructive, our team is equipped with the technology and training to provide exceptional care.

Tooth Extractions

Safe removal of impacted or problematic teeth, with IV sedation available.

Permanent, natural-looking tooth replacement for single or multiple missing teeth.

Restoring jawbone density to support implants or address bone loss.

Comprehensive treatment planning for extensive tooth loss or damage.

Advanced on-site imaging for precise surgical planning.

IV Sedation & Anesthesia

Comfortable, monitored sedation options administered by our surgeons.

Orthognathic Surgery

Corrective jaw surgery for functional and alignment concerns.

Oral Pathology & Biopsies

Diagnosis and evaluation of unusual lesions or abnormalities.

Surgical exposure to guide teeth into proper position.

Facial Trauma & Fractures

Treatment for injuries to the jaw, cheekbones, and surrounding structures.


## What to Expect on Your First Visit


We understand that oral surgery can feel daunting, and we work to make your first visit as comfortable and informative as possible. Here is how a typical consultation unfolds at our Wilshire Boulevard office.

Arrival & Intake

You are greeted and guided through your intake. Complete patient registration online in advance to save time.

Imaging

Your surgeon evaluates your condition using our in-house Cone Beam 3D imaging — no outside referral needed.

Consultation

Your surgeon reviews your history, discusses sedation preferences, answers your questions, and walks you through all options.

Your Treatment Plan

You leave with a clear plan and full confidence in your care team — no pressure, no surprises.


## Why Brentwood Residents Choose Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


Brentwood patients drive east on Wilshire, San Vicente, or Sunset for a reason. Our practice offers a combination of credentials, technology, and personalized attention that is difficult to find in a single practice.

Dual Board-Certified Surgeons

Both Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi hold credentials from the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, reflecting the highest standard in the field.

In-House Cone Beam 3D Imaging

Precise, low-radiation imaging completed on-site, eliminating referrals and delays.

Full Sedation Options

Our surgeons administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in-office for anxious patients and complex procedures.

Westside Location

Our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326 sits directly along the corridor connecting Brentwood to the rest of West Los Angeles.

Comprehensive Scope of Care

From routine extractions to full arch reconstruction and jaw surgery — one practice, no multiple referrals.


## Understanding the Cost of Oral Surgery in Brentwood


Ready to Schedule Your Consultation?

Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi provide personalized treatment plans at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, serving Brentwood and the surrounding Westside.

Request an Appointment or call (310) 846-8978

The cost of oral surgery varies based on the procedure, complexity, and whether sedation is involved. We believe cost should never be a barrier to getting the care you need, which is why we offer multiple options to fit different financial situations. Our team reviews your insurance coverage prior to your appointment and provides a clear breakdown of any expected out-of-pocket costs.

For patients without insurance or those requiring procedures not covered by their plan, we offer flexible payment options to help spread costs over time. You can also review our insurance and financing information online before your visit. We work with a wide range of PPO dental insurance plans and are happy to answer questions about coverage during your consultation.


## Frequently Asked Questions From Brentwood Patients


How far is Wilshire Oral Surgery from Brentwood?

Our office is located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. From most of Brentwood, the drive is approximately 5 to 10 minutes east along Wilshire Boulevard, depending on traffic. We are easily accessible via San Vicente Boulevard and Sunset Boulevard as well.

Do you offer sedation for oral surgery procedures?

Yes. Our surgeons are trained and licensed to administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in-office. We offer sedation for wisdom tooth removal, dental implant placement, bone grafting, and other procedures where patients prefer a more comfortable experience or where the complexity of the case warrants it.

What is the difference between an oral surgeon and a general dentist?

Oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete four to six years of hospital-based surgical residency training after dental school, giving them advanced skills in anesthesia, complex extractions, implant surgery, jaw surgery, and facial trauma. General dentists may perform basic extractions and simple implant placements, but cases with significant complexity, bone loss, or sedation requirements are typically referred to a specialist like our surgeons.

Do I need a referral from my dentist to schedule an appointment?

No referral is required to schedule a consultation at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. Many patients contact us directly after identifying a concern or receiving an initial recommendation from their dentist. If your dentist has provided X-rays or records, we encourage you to bring them to your first appointment.

How long is recovery after wisdom tooth removal?

Recovery after wisdom tooth extraction typically involves two to four days of rest, with most patients returning to normal activity within a week. Swelling and mild discomfort are common in the first 48 to 72 hours. We provide detailed post-operative instructions and are available to answer any questions that arise during your recovery.

Does insurance cover oral surgery?

Many dental and medical insurance plans provide at least partial coverage for oral surgery procedures, particularly when they are medically necessary. Wisdom tooth removal, biopsies, bone grafts related to trauma, and certain implant cases may be covered. We review your specific plan before your appointment and provide a clear explanation of what is covered. Visit our insurance and financing page for more information.

Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi bring board-level oral surgery credentials and years of hands-on surgical experience to every patient at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. Whether you need a single extraction or are exploring implants and jaw surgery, our team takes the time to understand your goals and build a treatment plan around your anatomy, timeline, and budget. We serve patients throughout the Westside from our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025.

To take the first step, request an appointment online or call us at (310) 846-8978. Our team is ready to answer your questions and help you understand your options. We also serve patients from Santa Monica and West Los Angeles, and you can view all the communities we serve on the Westside.

How far is Wilshire Oral Surgery from Century City?

What sedation options are available?

Oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete four to six years of hospital-based surgical residency training after dental school, giving them advanced skills in anesthesia, complex extractions, implant surgery, jaw surgery, and facial trauma. ## Frequently Asked Questions From Culver City Patients


How far is Wilshire Oral Surgery from Culver City?

Our office is located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. From central Culver City, the drive north via Sepulveda Boulevard or Overland Avenue to Wilshire typically takes ten to fifteen minutes depending on traffic. Patients can also reach us via the 405 Freeway northbound to the Wilshire Boulevard exit.

Do you offer sedation for oral surgery procedures?

Yes. Our surgeons are trained and licensed to administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in-office. We offer sedation for wisdom tooth removal, dental implant placement, bone grafting, and other procedures where patients prefer a more comfortable experience or where the complexity of the case warrants it.

What is the difference between an oral surgeon and a general dentist?

Oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete four to six years of hospital-based surgical residency training after dental school, giving them advanced skills in anesthesia, complex extractions, implant surgery, jaw surgery, and facial trauma. General dentists may perform basic extractions and simple implant placements, but cases with significant complexity, bone loss, or sedation requirements are typically referred to a specialist like our surgeons.

Do I need a referral from my dentist to schedule an appointment?

No referral is required to schedule a consultation at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. Many patients contact us directly after identifying a concern or receiving an initial recommendation from their dentist. If your dentist has provided X-rays or records, we encourage you to bring them to your first appointment.

How long is recovery after wisdom tooth removal?

Recovery after wisdom tooth extraction typically involves two to four days of rest, with most patients returning to normal activity within a week. Swelling and mild discomfort are common in the first 48 to 72 hours. We provide detailed post-operative instructions and are available to answer any questions that arise during your recovery.

Does insurance cover oral surgery?

Many dental and medical insurance plans provide at least partial coverage for oral surgery procedures, particularly when they are medically necessary. Wisdom tooth removal, biopsies, bone grafts related to trauma, and certain implant cases may be covered. We review your specific plan before your appointment and provide a clear explanation of what is covered. Visit our insurance and financing page for more information.

## Frequently Asked Questions From Mar Vista Patients


How far is Wilshire Oral Surgery from Mar Vista?

Do I need a referral to see an oral surgeon?

No referral is required to schedule a consultation at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. Many Mar Vista patients contact us directly after identifying a problem or receiving a recommendation from their general dentist. If your dentist has taken recent X-rays or provided records, bringing those to your appointment can help us plan more efficiently.

What sedation options are available for oral surgery?

We offer local anesthesia, IV sedation, and general anesthesia, all administered in-office by our surgeons. IV sedation and general anesthesia are appropriate for patients with dental anxiety, those undergoing multiple procedures in one visit, or complex cases requiring deeper anesthesia. Our team will discuss which option is safest and most appropriate for your specific procedure during your consultation.

How long does wisdom tooth removal recovery take?

Most patients recover from wisdom tooth removal within five to seven days, with the most noticeable swelling and discomfort occurring in the first two to three days. Patients who receive IV sedation will need a driver and should plan to rest the remainder of that day. We provide complete post-operative instructions and are available to answer recovery questions.

Does insurance cover dental implants or bone grafting?

Coverage varies by plan. Some PPO dental plans provide partial coverage for implant placement, particularly when tooth loss is the result of injury or a covered extraction. Bone grafting may be covered under medical insurance when it is linked to trauma or a medically necessary procedure. We review your specific plan before your appointment and provide a clear breakdown of covered versus out-of-pocket costs. See our insurance and financing page for more detail.

What makes an oral surgeon different from a general dentist for implants?

Oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete four to six years of accredited hospital surgical residency training after dental school, covering advanced anesthesia, complex implant cases, bone reconstruction, jaw surgery, and facial trauma. This depth of training is particularly important for patients with bone loss, anatomical challenges, or cases requiring sedation. General dentists can place implants in straightforward cases, but patients with more complex needs are typically best served by a board-certified oral surgeon. How far is Wilshire Oral Surgery from Palms?

Our office is located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. From Palms, heading north on Overland Avenue or Motor Avenue to Wilshire Boulevard typically puts you at our practice in around ten to fifteen minutes, depending on traffic. No freeway is required for most of the drive.

Do you offer sedation for oral surgery procedures?

Yes. Our surgeons are trained and licensed to administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in-office. We offer sedation for wisdom tooth removal, dental implant placement, bone grafting, and other procedures where patients prefer a more comfortable experience or where the complexity of the case warrants it.

What is the difference between an oral surgeon and a general dentist?

Oral and maxillofacial surgeons complete four to six years of hospital-based surgical residency training after dental school, giving them advanced skills in anesthesia, complex extractions, implant surgery, jaw surgery, and facial trauma. General dentists may perform basic extractions and simple implant placements, but cases with significant complexity, bone loss, or sedation requirements are typically referred to a specialist like our surgeons.

Do I need a referral from my dentist to schedule an appointment?

No referral is required to schedule a consultation at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. Many patients contact us directly after identifying a concern or receiving an initial recommendation from their dentist. How long is recovery after wisdom tooth removal?

Recovery after wisdom tooth extraction typically involves two to four days of rest, with most patients returning to normal activity within a week. Swelling and mild discomfort are common in the first 48 to 72 hours. We provide detailed post-operative instructions and are available to answer any questions that arise during your recovery.

Does insurance cover oral surgery?

Many dental and medical insurance plans provide at least partial coverage for oral surgery procedures, particularly when they are medically necessary. Wisdom tooth removal, biopsies, bone grafts related to trauma, and certain implant cases may be covered. ## How Wisdom Teeth Become a Problem in West LA Patients


Third molars are the last teeth to develop, usually between the late teens and mid-twenties. Because the modern jaw rarely provides adequate space for a full set of wisdom teeth, these teeth commonly become impacted, meaning they are prevented from erupting normally. Impaction leads to a range of clinical problems that worsen over time without intervention.

West LA’s younger professional and student population tends to delay this care until symptoms force the issue. A far better approach, supported by the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, is to evaluate wisdom teeth in the late teens or early twenties and remove them before root development is complete and surrounding bone becomes denser. Early removal leads to shorter procedures, faster recovery, and fewer complications.

Bone Impaction

The tooth is fully encased in bone and gum tissue. Surgical extraction requires removing bone to access and section the tooth.

Soft Tissue Impaction

The tooth has partially erupted through the bone but remains covered by gum tissue, creating a breeding ground for bacteria and infection.

Distal Angulation

The tooth grows at an angle tilted away from the second molar, which can damage the distal surface of that adjacent tooth over time.

Asymptomatic Impaction

No current symptoms, but imaging reveals positional or developmental factors that make removal advisable before complications develop.

How many days will I need off work for wisdom tooth removal?

Most patients take two to three days off and return to desk work by day four. What is the difference between a partially and fully impacted wisdom tooth?

A partially impacted tooth has broken through the overlying gum tissue to some degree but has not fully erupted into the mouth. A fully impacted tooth remains entirely within the bone or gum tissue with no visible presence in the mouth. Both types are removed surgically, though the approach varies based on position, angulation, and root anatomy.

What should I eat after wisdom tooth surgery?

For the first 24 hours, stick to soft foods and liquids that require minimal chewing, such as yogurt, smoothies, mashed potatoes, and soups at room temperature. Avoid hard, crunchy, or chewy foods for at least a week. Our post-operative care instructions include a detailed guide to diet and activity during recovery.

## Why Wisdom Teeth May Need to Come Out


Third molars, commonly called wisdom teeth, typically emerge between the ages of 17 and 25. Because the jaw is often too small to accommodate them fully, wisdom teeth may become impacted, meaning they are unable to erupt normally through the gumline. Impacted wisdom teeth can remain entirely beneath the bone, emerge at an angle that crowds adjacent teeth, or partially break through the gum in ways that create persistent infection risk.

Common reasons patients from Brentwood seek removal include pain or swelling at the back of the jaw, pressure behind the second molars, recurring infections around a partially erupted tooth, and recommendations from an orthodontist or general dentist following panoramic imaging. According to the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, the majority of young adults have at least one wisdom tooth that requires monitoring or removal. Earlier removal during the late teenage years or early twenties typically results in shorter recovery times, because root development is incomplete and the surrounding bone is more flexible.

Fully Impacted

Tooth is completely below the bone and gumline, causing pressure or cyst formation.

Partially Erupted

Tooth has broken through partially, creating a gum flap that traps bacteria and leads to pericoronitis.

Angularly Positioned

Tooth is growing sideways into the adjacent molar or at a forward angle, creating pressure and crowding.

Symptom-Free but Monitored

No current symptoms, but imaging reveals developing complications that make proactive removal advisable.

## Why Wisdom Teeth Require an Oral Surgeon


General dentists perform routine extractions, but wisdom teeth, particularly impacted ones, involve surgical access, bone removal, tooth sectioning, and proximity to critical nerves that require the training of an oral and maxillofacial surgeon. The inferior alveolar nerve, which runs through the lower jaw, can be within millimeters of lower wisdom tooth roots. Cone Beam 3D imaging lets us measure this relationship precisely before any instrument is used.

The American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons identifies impacted wisdom teeth as one of the most common oral surgery indications, particularly in younger adults. Board-certified surgeons like Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi have completed hospital-based residency training that included high volumes of impacted wisdom tooth cases across varying levels of complexity. That experience translates directly to a more predictable outcome and a more comfortable patient experience.

Mesioangular Impaction

The most common type. The tooth is angled toward the front of the mouth, pressing against the second molar. May cause crowding or root resorption.

Horizontal Impaction

The tooth lies completely on its side, pointing directly into the second molar’s root. More complex to extract and typically requires sectioning.

Vertical Impaction

The tooth is in a normal vertical position but has not fully erupted into the mouth. May cause infection risk at the gum flap even when no pain is present.

Distoangular Impaction

The tooth angles backward toward the rear of the jaw. Among the more technically challenging cases due to limited surgical access and proximity to nerves.

If you choose IV sedation, you will need a driver for the return trip to Century City or elsewhere, and you should plan to rest for the remainder of the day. When is the best time to have wisdom teeth removed?

The optimal window is typically in the late teens or early twenties, when root development is not yet complete and the surrounding bone is more flexible. However, wisdom tooth removal is performed successfully at any age. The main factors are the clinical indication, the anatomy of the teeth, and the patient’s overall health. We evaluate all of this at your consultation.

Can I go back to work the next day?

It depends on the nature of your work. Many patients doing desk or remote work can return by day two or three, though day one post-surgery is generally not recommended for any work activity. If your job involves physical labor or strenuous activity, a longer recovery period applies. We give you realistic expectations based on your specific case at your consultation.

What is the risk of nerve damage with lower wisdom teeth?

The inferior alveolar nerve runs through the lower jaw in close proximity to some patients’ wisdom tooth roots. We use Cone Beam 3D imaging to measure this relationship precisely before surgery. In cases where roots are extremely close to the nerve, we discuss the associated risk transparently and can adjust the surgical plan accordingly, including techniques that reduce nerve exposure.

Do I need to have all four wisdom teeth out at once?

Not necessarily, though removing all four at once is the most common approach because it means a single recovery period and a single sedation event. If you have strong clinical reasons to remove only specific teeth, we can discuss a phased approach. The right plan depends on your imaging and individual clinical situation.

What causes dry socket and how do I avoid it?

Dry socket occurs when the blood clot that forms in the extraction socket is dislodged or dissolves before the site heals. It is more common in smokers and patients who drink through straws. Our post-operative instructions include specific guidance on avoiding dry socket, and we are available for prompt follow-up care if any complications arise during healing.

## What Parents and Patients in Sawtelle Should Know About Wisdom Teeth


The recommendation to remove wisdom teeth often comes from an orthodontist or general dentist at a routine visit. Third molars are the last teeth to develop, typically between ages 17 and 25, and the modern jaw usually lacks the space to accommodate them. When they become impacted, they can cause ongoing infection, crowding, cyst formation, and damage to the adjacent second molars.

For parents coordinating care for a son or daughter, the most common questions are about timing, recovery expectations, and whether the procedure can be done in one appointment. For the patient, the anxiety about the procedure itself is often the primary concern. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we address both. The American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons recommends early evaluation, typically in the late teens, to allow for removal before roots are fully developed and recovery becomes more complex. Earlier removal means shorter procedures, faster healing, and fewer complications.

For Teenagers and Young Adults

Removal in the late teens often means shorter roots, less dense bone, and a recovery that is more predictable and faster than waiting until the mid-twenties or beyond.

For College Students Home on Break

Sawtelle’s proximity to our office means a student can have their consultation and procedure handled efficiently during a two-to-three week break without extended travel.

For Working Adults

Wisdom tooth pain and infection are unpredictable. A working adult who defers care often ends up managing an acute situation on a bad timeline. Proactive removal is almost always more convenient.

For Bilingual Households

Our team communicates in English, Spanish, and Farsi/Persian. Post-operative instructions, pre-surgical preparation, and follow-up can all be handled in your preferred language.


## The Procedure — What to Expect at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


Every wisdom tooth case begins with a consultation that includes a review of your existing X-rays or new Cone Beam 3D imaging taken in our office. This imaging shows the position, angulation, and root anatomy of each wisdom tooth and allows us to plan the surgical approach precisely. We explain what we find and answer your questions before anything is scheduled.

On the day of surgery, most patients choose IV sedation administered by our board-certified surgeons. The procedure typically takes under an hour for all four teeth. Patients wake with no memory of the surgery and begin their recovery at home. We provide complete post-operative care instructions and review our pre-operative guidelines well in advance so there are no surprises on the day of surgery. For sedation appointments, review our pre-anesthesia instructions carefully beforehand.

Consultation

We review your imaging or take in-house 3D imaging. A clear surgical plan and cost estimate are provided before your procedure is scheduled.

Pre-Op Prep

Pre-operative and anesthesia instructions are reviewed. Arrange a driver if choosing IV sedation. Fast as instructed.

Surgery

Procedure takes under an hour. IV sedation patients wake with little or no memory of the surgery and are driven home by a responsible adult.

Recovery at Home

Most patients feel significantly better by day three or four. Follow all post-operative care instructions and contact us with any questions during healing.

## Frequently Asked Questions — Wisdom Teeth Removal near Sawtelle


My teenager was referred for wisdom teeth removal — what is the first step?

The first step is a consultation at our office, which includes a review of any X-rays your general dentist or orthodontist has already taken, or new in-house 3D imaging if needed. We evaluate each tooth’s position and root development, explain what we find in plain language, and provide a clear recommendation and cost estimate before anything is scheduled.

Can a parent accompany a minor during the procedure?

A parent or legal guardian must be present for any minor patient and must provide consent for surgery. The parent or guardian is required to remain in the building during the procedure and to drive the patient home if IV sedation is used. Our staff will keep you informed and guide you through the process from arrival through discharge.

What is recovery like for a teenager compared to an adult?

Younger patients with less fully developed roots and less dense bone typically recover somewhat faster than older adults with fully mature wisdom teeth. Swelling and discomfort peak in the first 48 to 72 hours for both groups and then gradually improve. Most teenagers are significantly more comfortable by day three or four, similar to adult patients.

Do you offer bilingual consultations?

Yes. Our team communicates in English, Spanish, and Farsi/Persian. If you or your family member would prefer to receive pre-operative instructions, discuss the procedure, or ask post-operative questions in Spanish or Farsi, we can accommodate that throughout the entire care process.

Is your office actually in the Sawtelle neighborhood?

Yes. Our address is 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025, which is in the 90025 zip code that covers the Sawtelle corridor. Patients from the residential streets near Sawtelle Avenue and Olympic Boulevard can walk or take a very short drive to reach us.

How do I know if wisdom teeth removal is actually necessary?

The recommendation is based on imaging, not just symptoms. An impacted or poorly positioned wisdom tooth that causes no current pain may still be developing a problem that will become more complex and more difficult to treat over time. We review your imaging at your consultation and give you a clear, honest assessment of what we see and what we recommend — and why.

## Choosing the Right Window for Culver City Patients


The best time to have wisdom teeth removed is before they cause an acute problem. The American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons recommends evaluation in the late teens and early twenties, when root development is incomplete and bone is less dense, leading to faster, more predictable recovery. Patients in their late twenties and thirties still receive excellent outcomes, but root development and bone density differences can extend the recovery window slightly.

For Culver City professionals, the practical message is to schedule during a period when you can commit two to three days to rest and recovery. That window is the acute phase. Most patients are functional for desk or remote work by day three or four and cleared for all activity within a week. Planning that window around a production schedule, a hiatus, or a quiet patch on the calendar makes the experience far less disruptive than waiting for a symptom to force the issue at the worst possible moment.

Production Hiatus

A planned break in production provides a natural window for a procedure with a two-to-three day acute recovery. Schedule your consultation well in advance to secure the surgical date you need.

Long Weekend

A Thursday or Friday procedure gives four to five days of recovery before returning to office or set work, which is sufficient for many straightforward wisdom tooth extractions.

Summer or Holiday Break

Longer breaks offer the most flexibility. Many Culver City professionals handle longer-deferred procedures during summer or between December and January when studio activity slows.

Urgent Need

When infection or acute pain makes waiting impossible, we work to evaluate and treat urgent cases promptly. Do not delay if symptoms are escalating.

Every wisdom tooth case at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center begins with a detailed evaluation using Cone Beam 3D imaging. This technology gives us a three-dimensional view of each tooth’s position, root development, angulation, and proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve and other critical structures. We use this data to plan the surgical approach for each tooth before any instrument is used, which supports more predictable results and more informed patient consent.

Our complete pre-operative guidelines and pre-anesthesia instructions are provided well in advance so you arrive fully prepared. ## Frequently Asked Questions — Wisdom Teeth Removal near Culver City


How long is the drive from Culver City to your office?

From central Culver City, the drive to our office via Sepulveda Boulevard or National Boulevard heading north to Wilshire is typically 10 to 15 minutes. Our address is 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. Building parking is available.

Can I book a consultation and surgery appointment on the same day?

Same-day consultation and surgery is possible when the clinical situation allows, the fasting requirement for sedation can be met, and surgical availability exists. Contact our office in advance to discuss whether this is feasible for your case. When same-day surgery is not available, we work to minimize the gap between consultation and procedure for patients with tight scheduling windows.

How many days off should I plan for?

Plan for the day of surgery plus two full days of rest for most straightforward cases. Day three and four typically see significant improvement, and most patients doing sedentary creative or professional work are functional by day three. Physical activity, heavy lifting, and anything that raises blood pressure should be avoided for a full week.

What if I have dental insurance through a studio or streaming company?

We work with all major PPO dental carriers. Studio and streaming company dental plans are typically through Aetna, Delta Dental, Cigna, or MetLife, all of which we work with. We verify your specific plan benefits before scheduling surgery. Contact our office with your insurance information before your consultation to confirm participation.

My wisdom teeth are not hurting — do I still need to have them removed?

Not always, but symptoms are not a reliable indicator of clinical need. Many impacted wisdom teeth develop problems without causing noticeable pain until the problem is advanced. We evaluate each tooth on its own imaging — position, angulation, root proximity to nerves, and whether any pathology is developing — and make a recommendation based on clinical evidence rather than symptoms alone.

Is it safe to have all four wisdom teeth removed at once?

For most patients, removing all four at once under IV sedation is the most efficient and clinically sensible approach, as it means a single recovery period instead of two or more separate procedures. Our surgeons evaluate your case individually and discuss whether a phased approach is preferable based on your specific anatomy, health history, and circumstances.

Impaction is determined through imaging, not symptoms alone. Your dentist or orthodontist may have already identified this on a panoramic X-ray. We confirm and characterize impaction using our in-house 3D imaging at the consultation.

## What First-Time Patients Should Know About Wisdom Teeth


Third molars are the last set of permanent teeth to develop, usually beginning to emerge between the ages of 17 and 25. Most people’s jaws do not have adequate space for all four, which leads to impaction. An impacted wisdom tooth is one that cannot fully erupt into its normal position, whether because of bone, adjacent teeth, or its own growth angle. Left in place, impacted wisdom teeth can cause infection, cyst formation, crowding, and damage to neighboring roots.

The American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons recommends evaluation in the late teens or early twenties while roots are still developing and bone is less dense, which leads to shorter, more predictable procedures and faster recovery. For Palms patients who are in that window and have already received a referral from their dentist or orthodontist, the right next step is a consultation with a board-certified oral surgeon, not further delay.

Impaction = Surgical Removal

Impacted wisdom teeth require a surgical approach — local or IV sedation, removal of overlying tissue and sometimes bone, and tooth sectioning in many cases. This is routine for an oral surgeon.

Earlier Is Easier

Root development in the late teens means shorter, less curved roots and softer surrounding bone. Recovery is typically faster and the procedure is less complex than waiting until the mid-twenties or later.

Sedation Makes It Manageable

Most patients choose IV sedation and have no memory of the procedure. Anxiety about the surgery itself is the most common concern — sedation addresses it directly and effectively.

Insurance Usually Applies

PPO dental plans typically cover wisdom tooth removal, especially for impacted teeth. We verify coverage before scheduling so you know the cost before committing.

## Dental Implants in West Los Angeles — Your Neighborhood Oral Surgery Practice


Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is not just near West Los Angeles. We are part of it. Our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025 sits squarely in the 90025 zip code, surrounded by the employers, neighborhoods, and communities that define West LA.
