For the professionals working at Google’s Los Angeles campus, Hulu, and UCLA Health who make up much of the local patient base, a lunchtime consultation or a post-workday appointment is genuinely feasible.

Dental implants are among the most technically demanding procedures in dentistry, and the credential level of the surgeon matters significantly for outcomes. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, implant surgery is performed exclusively by Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi, both board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons with hospital residency training and hands-on experience in complex implant cases.


## The Case for Implants in the West LA Market


West Los Angeles patients are accustomed to evaluating their healthcare options carefully. When it comes to tooth replacement, implants stand apart from bridges and removable partial dentures in ways that matter long-term. A titanium implant integrates with the jawbone through osseointegration, providing root-level support that stimulates bone and prevents the progressive resorption that follows tooth loss. A bridge avoids this by resting on adjacent teeth, which must be reduced to serve as anchors. A partial denture avoids bone contact altogether, leaving the underlying ridge to resorb over time.

For West LA patients who intend to keep their oral health at a high level for decades, the implant is typically the best long-term investment. According to the National Library of Medicine, implant dentistry is among the most well-documented tooth replacement modalities available, with a clinical track record built over more than four decades.

Single Implant

Replaces one tooth root-to-crown without altering adjacent teeth. The standard of care for isolated tooth loss in healthy bone.

Multiple Implants

Two or more implants placed at adjacent or distributed sites. Can support individual crowns or an implant-supported bridge.

Full-Arch Restoration

For patients missing most or all teeth in one arch, four to six implants support a complete, fixed prosthesis in a single surgical phase.

Ridge Augmentation

When bone volume has been lost prior to implant planning, ridge augmentation rebuilds the site to prepare for a stable, long-term implant.


## Technology That Changes the Outcome


Implant placement is not a procedure where guesswork serves anyone well. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we use Cone Beam 3D imaging to generate a precise three-dimensional map of each implant site before we plan a single incision. This technology shows bone density, width, height, root proximity to adjacent teeth, and the precise location of nerves and sinus structures that must be avoided.

The surgical plan is built around this data, not modified to fit it after the fact. For West LA patients who appreciate technology-forward healthcare, this is the planning standard you would expect. When bone grafting is necessary before placement, we perform that as well, often on the same visit using platelet-rich fibrin to support faster healing. Full post-operative care is covered by our detailed post-operative instructions.

The major employers in West Los Angeles, including Google, Hulu, Amazon Studios, Cedars-Sinai, and UCLA Health, maintain comprehensive employer-sponsored dental PPO plans. Dr. Jonathan R. Dr. Saman Vahedi holds a Diplomate credential from the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, the specialty’s highest designation, and completed his residency training at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, where he served as Chief Resident in 2013 and 2014. ## Frequently Asked Questions — Dental Implants near West Los Angeles


Where exactly is your West LA office?

We are located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025, in a four-story office building on the south side of Wilshire between McClellan Drive and Wellesley Avenue. Parking is available in the building. The office is within walking distance of Sawtelle and a short drive from anywhere in the 90025 and 90064 zip codes.

Can I come in for a consultation during the workday?

Yes. We offer appointment availability to accommodate working professionals and schedule consultations with this in mind. Contact our office to discuss timing that works with your schedule. Same-day consultations are sometimes available when clinical circumstances allow.

Does my employer dental plan cover implants?

Coverage depends on your specific plan design. Many employer-sponsored PPO plans in West LA, particularly those from large tech, media, and healthcare employers, include some implant coverage when the procedure is medically indicated. We verify your benefits prior to any scheduled procedure and give you a clear cost estimate upfront.

What is osseointegration and how long does it take?

Osseointegration is the biological process by which the titanium implant fuses with the surrounding jawbone, creating a stable, permanent anchor for the crown. This process typically takes three to six months and is largely passive from the patient’s perspective. Daily activity is not significantly affected during this period.

What if I don’t have enough bone for an implant?

Insufficient bone is one of the most common reasons patients are told an implant is not possible at their current dentist. In many cases, a bone grafting procedure can rebuild the site adequately for implant placement. We evaluate bone volume using Cone Beam 3D imaging and discuss the options, including timing and whether grafting can be done simultaneously with implant placement.

Do you offer full-arch implant restoration?

Yes. For patients who are missing most or all of their teeth in one arch, full-arch restoration using four to six implants to support a fixed prosthesis is available. This is sometimes referred to as “teeth in a day” or All-on-X. We discuss candidacy, timeline, and costs thoroughly during your consultation.

# Dental Implants near Brentwood CA


Home › Areas We Serve › Dental Implants near Brentwood, CA


## Dental Implants for Brentwood Patients, Minutes from Wilshire Boulevard


If you are looking for dental implants near Brentwood, CA, Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is one of the closest board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgery practices to your neighborhood. Our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025 is approximately 1.2 miles from the heart of Brentwood. A short drive east along Wilshire Boulevard or San Vicente puts you at our door without any freeway required. For Brentwood residents, UCLA families, and professionals working along the corridor, we offer the full scope of implant dentistry in a modern, efficient setting.

Dental implants are one of the most consequential procedures we perform, and the quality of the surgical team matters. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, implant surgery is performed by two board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons who have completed hospital-based training and hold the highest clinical credentials in the specialty.


## What Makes a Dental Implant the Right Choice


A dental implant replaces a missing tooth at the root level, providing a stable titanium foundation that integrates with the surrounding jawbone through a process called osseointegration. Once integrated, a custom crown is placed on top, restoring the full appearance and function of a natural tooth. Unlike a bridge, an implant does not require reducing adjacent healthy teeth. Unlike a removable partial denture, an implant is fixed in place and does not shift during eating or speaking.

Patients from Brentwood seek implants for a range of reasons, including tooth loss from decay, fracture, or failed prior restorations, as well as planned extractions where the tooth cannot be saved. According to the National Library of Medicine, dental implants have become a standard treatment modality in dentistry with well-established long-term outcomes when placed by trained surgeons. Early consultation is important because bone preservation is optimal when an implant is placed shortly after tooth loss.

Single-Tooth Implant

Replaces one missing tooth with a titanium post and custom crown. No impact on adjacent healthy teeth.

Implant-Supported Bridge

Two implants support a fixed bridge to replace two or more consecutive missing teeth without a removable appliance.

Full-Arch Restoration

Four to six implants support a full arch of fixed teeth, replacing an entire upper or lower row in one surgical phase.

When bone volume is insufficient for implant placement, a grafting procedure rebuilds the ridge before or at the time of implant surgery.


## The Implant Process at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


The implant process typically begins with a consultation and Cone Beam 3D imaging to assess bone volume, tooth position, and anatomy. Our surgeons use this precise three-dimensional imaging to plan placement angle, depth, and position before any surgery begins. This planning step reduces guesswork and allows for a more predictable surgical outcome.

If bone grafting is required due to atrophy or prior extraction socket loss, that procedure is typically completed first and allowed to heal before implant placement. In cases where bone volume is adequate, implant placement and grafting can sometimes occur simultaneously. After the implant integrates with the bone over a healing period, your general dentist or prosthodontist places the final crown. We coordinate closely with referring providers throughout this process.

Consultation and Imaging

We evaluate bone volume, tooth anatomy, and overall oral health using Cone Beam 3D imaging before recommending a surgical plan.

Bone Grafting (if needed)

If bone volume is insufficient, we perform bone grafting to create a stable foundation. Healing time varies by graft type and volume.

Implant Placement

The titanium implant is placed under IV sedation or local anesthesia depending on the case. Most patients resume normal activity within a few days.

Final Restoration

After osseointegration, your referring dentist or our team completes the crown or prosthesis. We provide detailed post-operative care instructions throughout.


## IV Sedation Options for Implant Surgery


Implant surgery is performed under local anesthesia for most straightforward cases. For patients who prefer a deeper level of comfort, or for more complex procedures involving multiple implants or simultaneous bone grafting, IV sedation is available. Our board-certified surgeons administer sedation directly, which keeps the process streamlined and cost-effective compared to a separate hospital setting. Under IV sedation, you remain deeply relaxed throughout the procedure with no memory of the surgical experience. You will need a responsible adult to drive you home and stay with you for the first few hours after surgery.


## Understanding the Cost of Dental Implants near Brentwood


The cost of dental implants in the Los Angeles area varies based on the number of implants needed, whether bone grafting is required, the complexity of the case, and your insurance coverage. PPO dental plans may provide partial coverage for implant-related procedures, particularly when the implant is replacing a tooth lost due to trauma, infection, or a medically necessary extraction. We verify your benefits before your procedure so there are no surprises.

For patients who require financing, we offer flexible payment options to help manage the cost of care. We also provide itemized estimates before any treatment begins. Visit our insurance and financing page for more detail on how we handle coverage verification and patient billing.


## Our Surgeons — Board-Certified Implant Expertise Serving Brentwood


Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is led by two board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons with deep roots on the Westside. Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi earned his undergraduate degree in neuroscience at UCLA and his DDS at the USC School of Dentistry, where he graduated on the Dean’s List and received the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. Dr. Saman Vahedi completed both his undergraduate education and dental training at UCLA and USC, then went on to complete a hospital-based oral and maxillofacial surgery residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, where he served as Chief Resident in 2013 and 2014. Dr. Vahedi holds Diplomate status with the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, the highest credential in the field.


## Frequently Asked Questions — Dental Implants near Brentwood


How far is Wilshire Oral Surgery from Brentwood?

Our office is approximately 1.2 miles from the center of Brentwood, located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. Most patients drive east along Wilshire Boulevard and arrive in under 10 minutes without any freeway required.

Who performs the implant surgery?

All implant surgeries at our practice are performed by Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi or Dr. Saman Vahedi, both of whom are board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons with hospital-based residency training. Dr. Vahedi is a Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons.

Do I need a bone graft before getting an implant?

Not all patients require bone grafting. Whether a graft is needed depends on the volume and density of bone at the implant site, which we assess using Cone Beam 3D imaging during your consultation. If grafting is required, we discuss the timeline and options with you before any treatment begins.

Can I be sedated for implant surgery?

Yes. We offer IV sedation administered by our board-certified surgeons for patients who prefer a deeper level of comfort or for complex multi-implant cases. Most patients who receive IV sedation have no memory of the procedure. A responsible adult must drive you home and stay with you for the first few hours after surgery.

Does PPO dental insurance cover dental implants?

Coverage varies significantly by plan. Some PPO plans provide partial coverage for implant placement, particularly when the tooth was lost due to a covered condition such as trauma or infection. We verify your benefits before your appointment and provide a clear estimate of out-of-pocket costs before any procedure begins.

How long does implant recovery take?

Most patients return to normal activity within two to three days of implant placement. Osseointegration, the process by which the implant fuses with the bone, takes several months. We provide detailed post-operative care instructions and remain available for follow-up throughout the healing process.

## Dental Implants for Santa Monica Patients — Board-Certified Surgeons on the Wilshire Corridor


Santa Monica residents looking for dental implants have options, but few practices along the corridor can match the clinical credentials and technology available at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. Our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025 sits at the eastern end of the Wilshire corridor, reachable from Santa Monica in roughly 10 to 15 minutes by car heading east. For patients who live near Ocean Avenue, Montana Avenue, or Pico Boulevard, the drive is direct and involves no freeway. For those closer to the I-10, access via the 405 or Olympic Boulevard is equally straightforward.

Santa Monica draws a patient base that includes tech and entertainment professionals, healthcare workers from Providence Saint John’s Health Center and UCLA Health clinics, and a large population of health-conscious adults who want expert care with minimal disruption to their schedules. Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is designed around that mindset. Learn about our surgeons and our approach to treatment before you schedule your consultation.


## Why Santa Monica Patients Choose Implants Over Other Options


A dental implant is not just a cosmetic decision. For many patients, it is the difference between preserving jawbone density long-term and experiencing progressive bone loss that limits future treatment options. When a tooth is lost, the bone that once supported it begins to resorb within months. An implant, which acts as an artificial root, stimulates the bone and halts that process in a way that bridges and dentures cannot.

For Santa Monica patients who value longevity in their healthcare decisions, an implant typically represents the best long-term investment. It does not involve reducing adjacent healthy teeth the way a bridge does, and it does not require adhesives or overnight removal the way a partial denture does. According to the National Library of Medicine, dental implants are one of the most well-documented tooth replacement options available, with outcomes established over decades of clinical research.

Preserves Bone

An implant stimulates the jawbone just like a natural root, preventing the bone resorption that begins within months of tooth loss.

No Impact on Adjacent Teeth

Unlike a traditional bridge, an implant does not require grinding down neighboring healthy teeth to serve as anchors.

Fixed in Place

An implant-supported crown functions like a natural tooth. It does not shift, click, or require removal for cleaning the way a partial denture does.

Long-Term Solution

With proper care, implants are designed to last decades. They are built to integrate permanently with the surrounding bone.


## Our Implant Process From Consultation to Crown


The first step is a consultation that includes a clinical evaluation and Cone Beam 3D imaging of the implant site. This imaging gives us a precise three-dimensional view of your bone volume, root proximity, and anatomy, which we use to plan placement before any surgery begins. We share the imaging findings with you and explain the recommended approach clearly before you commit to any treatment.

If your bone volume at the implant site is insufficient, a bone grafting procedure may be recommended prior to implant placement. Once adequate bone is present, the titanium implant is placed surgically under local anesthesia or IV sedation. After a healing period for osseointegration, your general dentist or prosthodontist completes the final crown, which we coordinate closely with your referring provider throughout.

Consultation + 3D Imaging

We assess bone volume, anatomy, and overall health. You receive a clear treatment plan before any procedure is scheduled.

Bone Graft (if needed)

If bone volume is inadequate, grafting rebuilds the site. Healing time depends on graft size and whether placement is simultaneous.

Implant Placement

The titanium implant is placed surgically. Recovery for most patients is two to three days before returning to normal activity.

Crown Placement

After osseointegration, your final crown is placed. We provide post-operative care instructions and coordinate with your referring dentist.

The cost of dental implants depends on the number of implants, whether bone grafting is required, and your insurance coverage. Many PPO plans accepted in the Santa Monica area, including Delta Dental, Aetna, Cigna, and Blue Cross Blue Shield, provide partial coverage for implant-related procedures when they are medically indicated. We verify your benefits before scheduling surgery and provide itemized estimates upfront.

For costs not covered by insurance, we offer flexible payment options through CareCredit, Alphaeon, and Cherry financing. You can also review our insurance and financing page for a full overview of how we handle billing and coverage verification for Santa Monica and Westside patients.

Implant surgery at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is performed exclusively by our two board-certified surgeons. Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi earned his bachelor’s degree in neuroscience at UCLA and his DDS at the USC School of Dentistry, graduating on the Dean’s List and receiving the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. Dr. Saman Vahedi, a Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, completed his residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, where he served as Chief Resident in 2013 and 2014. Both surgeons bring hospital-trained precision to every case.

## Frequently Asked Questions — Dental Implants near Santa Monica


How long is the drive from Santa Monica to your office?

Most patients from Santa Monica reach our office in 10 to 15 minutes heading east on Wilshire Boulevard or Olympic Boulevard. There is no freeway required. Our address is 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025, which is near the corner of Wilshire and Bundy.

How many implants will I need?

This depends on how many teeth are missing and the condition of your remaining teeth and jawbone. A single missing tooth requires one implant. Multiple missing teeth may be replaced with individual implants or with an implant-supported bridge. We assess this during your consultation and make a recommendation based on your imaging and clinical findings.

Will I need a bone graft before my implant?

Not all patients do. A bone graft is needed when there is insufficient bone volume to securely support an implant. This is more common when a tooth has been missing for some time and bone resorption has occurred. We determine this through Cone Beam 3D imaging at your consultation.

Does Delta Dental cover dental implants in California?

Some Delta Dental PPO plans provide partial coverage for implant-related procedures, particularly when the implant replaces a tooth lost due to a covered condition. Coverage varies significantly by plan and employer. We contact your insurer before your procedure to verify exactly what is covered and what your estimated out-of-pocket cost will be.

Can I finance my implant treatment?

Yes. We work with CareCredit, Alphaeon, and Cherry financing, all of which offer payment plans designed for elective and surgical dental procedures. Many plans have low-interest or deferred-interest options depending on your creditworthiness. We can walk you through financing options at your consultation.

How long does recovery take after implant surgery?

Most patients return to normal daily activity within two to three days of the implant placement procedure. The longer healing process involves osseointegration, where the implant fuses with the surrounding bone, which typically takes three to six months. This phase is largely passive and does not affect your daily routine.

## The Science of Dental Implants — What Westwood Patients Should Know


A dental implant is a titanium post that is surgically placed into the jawbone to serve as an artificial root. Once placed, it undergoes osseointegration, a biological process in which bone cells grow into and around the titanium surface, anchoring the implant permanently. A crown is then placed on top, restoring the tooth’s appearance and function. The implant does not rely on adjacent teeth for support, does not require adhesive, and does not need to be removed for cleaning.

Bone preservation is one of the most clinically significant advantages of implants over other tooth replacement options. When a tooth is lost, the bone that supported it begins to resorb in the absence of mechanical stimulation. An implant provides that stimulation, halting the resorption process that would otherwise continue under a bridge or denture. The National Library of Medicine documents dental implants as a well-established treatment modality in dentistry with clinical outcomes supported by decades of evidence.

Osseointegration

Bone cells grow into the titanium surface over three to six months, permanently anchoring the implant without cement, screws through adjacent teeth, or adhesive.

Bone Preservation

The implant provides mechanical stimulation to the jawbone, preventing the resorption that begins within months of tooth loss and continues progressively under conventional restorations.

Structural Independence

The implant is self-supporting and does not require reducing, crowning, or loading adjacent healthy teeth — a meaningful long-term advantage over bridges.

Long Clinical Track Record

Implant dentistry is supported by more than four decades of clinical research. Outcomes data from multicenter studies inform current surgical techniques and protocols.

We use Cone Beam 3D imaging for every implant case. This technology creates a precise three-dimensional map of the surgical site, showing bone density, width, height, root positions, and the exact location of nerves and sinus anatomy. We use this data to plan each implant’s position, angle, and depth before any surgical procedure begins, reducing variability and improving predictability.

If bone volume at the implant site is insufficient due to prior tooth loss or atrophy, bone grafting can rebuild the site prior to or concurrent with implant placement. When appropriate, we also use platelet-rich fibrin to support healing at the surgical site. After integration, your referring general dentist or prosthodontist places the final crown, and we coordinate with your provider throughout the process. What is the success rate of dental implants?

Clinical research documents high long-term implant survival rates in healthy patients with adequate bone, though specific rates vary by study, implant system, location in the mouth, and patient health factors. What happens if an implant fails?

## Why Dental Implants Are the Right Long-Term Choice


Sawtelle patients who lose a tooth face the same decision as any patient: replace it with a bridge, a partial denture, or a dental implant. Of these options, a dental implant is the only one that replaces the tooth at the root level, stimulates the jawbone to prevent bone loss, and functions identically to a natural tooth without affecting adjacent healthy teeth. According to the National Library of Medicine, dental implants are among the most well-documented restorative options in dentistry, with a decades-long clinical record supporting their effectiveness.

Bridges replace the visible tooth but require reducing the adjacent teeth on either side to serve as anchors. Partial dentures restore function but are removable, can shift or require adhesive, and do nothing to preserve the underlying bone. For patients who want a solution they do not have to think about, clean any differently from natural teeth, or replace periodically, an implant is consistently the better long-term choice.

Preserves Neighboring Teeth

An implant stands independently. No adjacent teeth are reduced or used as anchors, meaning your healthy neighboring teeth remain completely intact.

Prevents Bone Loss

The titanium implant stimulates the jawbone through osseointegration, stopping the bone resorption that begins after tooth loss and accelerates under bridges and dentures.

No Maintenance Difference

An implant-supported crown is brushed and flossed like a natural tooth. No removals, no adhesives, no overnight soaking.

Designed to Last Decades

Implants are intended as a permanent solution. With proper care, the implant fixture itself rarely requires replacement, unlike a bridge that typically needs replacement eventually.

## Dental Implants for Culver City Patients — Board-Certified Oral Surgeons a Short Drive North


Culver City has evolved into one of Los Angeles’s most dynamic professional hubs, home to Sony Pictures, Apple TV+, Amazon MGM Studios, and a growing cluster of creative industry employers that draw a health-conscious, professionally ambitious workforce. Dental health decisions for this population tend to be deliberate and long-term. When it comes to replacing a missing tooth, that mindset consistently points toward dental implants over temporary or compromise solutions. Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center is located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025, approximately four to five miles north of Culver City’s core via Sepulveda Boulevard or National Boulevard, typically a 10 to 15 minute drive depending on traffic.

Our board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons bring hospital residency-level precision to every implant case, backed by in-house Cone Beam 3D imaging and IV sedation capability managed by the surgical team itself. For Culver City professionals who want thorough, credential-backed care without hospital scheduling complexity, we are the practice to call.


## Why Culver City Patients Invest in Dental Implants


A dental implant is not just a cosmetic restoration. It is a root-level intervention that replaces the full biological function of a natural tooth, preserves the jawbone at the site of loss, and protects adjacent healthy teeth from the structural compromise that comes with traditional bridges. For Culver City’s entertainment and tech professionals, who often include dental care in their overall health investment strategy, the implant’s long-term durability and low maintenance profile are significant advantages.

Research through the National Library of Medicine documents dental implants as one of the most rigorously studied and clinically supported tooth replacement modalities in modern dentistry. The outcomes data built over more than four decades supports implants as the standard of care for single and multiple tooth replacement in healthy bone.

Bone Preservation

The implant provides root-level stimulation that prevents the progressive bone resorption that begins within months of tooth loss and continues under bridges and dentures.

Zero Impact on Adjacent Teeth

Implants are structurally independent. Unlike a bridge, the adjacent healthy teeth are not reduced or used as anchors, preserving their full structural integrity.

No Ongoing Maintenance Burden

An implant-supported crown is brushed and flossed exactly like a natural tooth. No special tools, no removal, no adhesive. It integrates seamlessly into a normal oral care routine.

Long-Term Value

Implants are designed for permanence. The upfront investment reflects a solution that avoids the periodic replacement and downstream dental complications of other restorations.


## Technology and Planning That Support Precision Outcomes


Implant outcomes are only as reliable as the planning that precedes them. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, every implant case begins with Cone Beam 3D imaging that maps the bone volume, nerve location, sinus anatomy, and root positions at the implant site with millimeter-level precision. The surgical plan is built around this data before any procedure is scheduled, and we walk you through the findings clearly before you commit to anything.

When bone grafting is required prior to or concurrent with implant placement, we perform that procedure as well, sometimes with platelet-rich fibrin to support faster healing. IV sedation is available for the implant procedure and any associated surgical steps, administered by our board-certified surgeons in-office. After osseointegration is confirmed, your general dentist or prosthodontist places the final crown, and we coordinate with your referring provider throughout. Our post-operative care instructions guide each phase of recovery.

Consultation + Imaging

Cone Beam 3D imaging, bone assessment, and a complete treatment plan with timeline and cost estimate provided before any procedure is scheduled.

Grafting if Needed

When bone volume is insufficient, bone grafting builds the implant foundation. May be done separately or concurrent with placement.

Implant Placement

Placed under local anesthesia or IV sedation. Most Culver City patients return to their professional schedule within two to three days.

Final Crown

After osseointegration, your restorative dentist places the crown. The implant is permanently integrated and requires no special maintenance going forward.

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi completed his neuroscience degree at UCLA and his DDS at the USC School of Dentistry, graduating on the Dean’s List and earning the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. ## Frequently Asked Questions — Dental Implants near Culver City


What is the best route from Culver City to your office?

From central Culver City, Sepulveda Boulevard heading north to Wilshire Boulevard is the most direct route, typically 10 to 15 minutes without heavy traffic. National Boulevard to Bundy is another option. Our address is 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025. Building parking is available.

Can I schedule around a production or studio schedule?

We accommodate professional schedules and understand that Culver City patients often work in industries with irregular or intensive timelines. Contact our office to discuss availability that fits your production or work calendar. Most implant consultations are under 90 minutes, and the surgical procedure itself typically requires only a single appointment.

How soon can I go back to work after implant placement?

Most patients return to desk or office work within two to three days of the implant procedure. If you had IV sedation, the day of surgery should be reserved for rest. Strenuous physical activity and anything that significantly raises blood pressure should be avoided for at least a week. Creative and production work that is sedentary can typically resume by day three.

Do you handle both the implant and the crown?

We perform the surgical phase — implant placement, any bone grafting, and related procedures. The final crown is placed by your general dentist or prosthodontist after osseointegration is confirmed. We communicate and coordinate closely with your restorative provider throughout the process so the handoff is seamless.

What happens during the osseointegration phase?

Osseointegration is the period during which bone cells grow into and around the titanium implant surface, creating a permanent biological bond. This typically takes three to six months. During this phase, the implant site is largely unobtrusive. You continue your normal activities with no significant restrictions after the initial post-surgical recovery period of two to three days.

What if I’ve had a tooth missing for years — is it too late for an implant?

Years of tooth loss often mean some bone resorption has occurred at the site, but this does not necessarily prevent implant placement. We evaluate bone volume using Cone Beam 3D imaging and determine whether bone grafting is needed to create an adequate foundation. Many patients who assumed it was too late are good candidates after a grafting procedure.

An implant, which integrates with the bone through osseointegration, does.

For Mar Vista patients who want their oral health decisions to hold up over decades rather than require revision every few years, the implant is consistently the better investment. The National Library of Medicine documents dental implants as one of the most well-supported and widely studied options in restorative dentistry, with clinical outcomes data built over more than forty years of use.

Stops Bone Loss

Do I need a referral to see an oral surgeon for an implant?

No referral is required to schedule a consultation with us. Many patients come in directly after being told by their general dentist that they need an implant or after deciding on their own to explore options. If your dentist has already taken X-rays, you are welcome to bring them. We can also take our own in-house 3D imaging at your consultation.

What is the difference between a dental implant and a bridge?

A bridge replaces the visible tooth by spanning the gap and anchoring to the adjacent teeth on either side, which must be reduced and crowned in the process. An implant replaces the tooth at the root level without touching neighboring teeth. Implants also prevent jawbone resorption, which continues unaddressed under a bridge.

Are implants covered by my dental insurance?

Can I eat normally after the implant is placed?

In the first few days, soft foods are recommended to avoid stressing the surgical site. As healing progresses over the following weeks, you can gradually return to a normal diet. During the osseointegration phase, we recommend avoiding hard, crunchy, or very chewy foods directly on the implant site until the crown is placed and integration is confirmed.

Yes. IV sedation is available for implant placement and is administered by our board-certified oral surgeons in-office. Placed under local anesthesia or IV sedation at our West LA office. Most patients return to normal activity within two to three days.

After osseointegration, your restorative dentist places the crown. We coordinate throughout and provide full post-operative guidance.

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi trained at UCLA for his neuroscience degree and USC School of Dentistry for his DDS, earning the Dean’s List distinction and the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. How much does a dental implant cost in the Palms and West LA area?

The cost depends on the number of implants, whether bone grafting is required, and what your insurance covers. We provide a full itemized estimate at your consultation after reviewing your imaging and verifying your benefits. We do not quote costs without evaluating your specific case, because the range is meaningful depending on your individual situation.

Do you offer payment plans for dental implants?

Yes. We work with CareCredit, Alphaeon, and Cherry, all of which offer installment plans designed for high-value dental and medical procedures. Promotional low-interest and deferred-interest options are often available depending on your creditworthiness. We walk you through the financing options at your consultation alongside your insurance estimate.

Is an implant consultation free?

Please contact our office directly to ask about consultation fees and what is included. Some consultations may include in-house imaging. We are happy to answer your questions over the phone before you schedule.

How long does osseointegration take?

Osseointegration, the process by which the implant fuses with your jawbone, typically takes three to six months. During this period, daily activity is largely unaffected after the initial post-surgical recovery of two to three days. You are not sidelined for months — the healing is largely passive and does not interfere with your normal routine.

Can I get an implant if my tooth has been missing for several years?

Yes, in many cases. Long-term tooth loss leads to bone resorption, which may require a bone grafting procedure before implant placement. We evaluate the extent of bone loss using Cone Beam 3D imaging and give you an honest assessment of what is needed and whether it is feasible at your consultation. Many patients who assumed they had waited too long are good candidates after grafting.

Will my regular dentist place the crown?

Yes. Our role is to perform the surgical phase, including implant placement and any bone grafting. Your general dentist or prosthodontist places the final crown after osseointegration is confirmed. We communicate with your provider throughout the process and provide them with complete documentation of the implant position and specifications for a smooth handoff.

## Full-Arch Implant Restoration for West Los Angeles Patients


For patients in West Los Angeles who are missing most or all of their teeth in one arch, or who are facing imminent loss of failing dentition, full-arch implant restoration represents a fundamentally different category of treatment than individual implants. Using four to six titanium implants to support a fixed, full-arch prosthesis, this approach replaces an entire row of teeth in a single surgical phase. Patients sometimes hear this referred to as All-on-4, Teeth in a Day, or full-arch implants. Regardless of the name, the goal is the same: restoring full-arch function and appearance with a fixed, non-removable result supported by implants embedded in your own bone.

Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center performs full-arch implant procedures from our office at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326, Los Angeles, CA 90025, serving West LA patients who want board-certified surgical expertise and in-house imaging without traveling to a hospital or specialty center.


## Who Is a Candidate for Full-Arch Implant Restoration?


Full-arch implant restoration is designed for patients who have significant tooth loss, failing teeth that cannot be individually restored, or who are currently wearing or about to need a full denture. It is not appropriate for all patients, and candidacy depends on bone volume at the surgical sites, systemic health factors, and the patient’s specific goals and expectations.

We evaluate candidacy using Cone Beam 3D imaging to assess bone volume throughout the arch. Some patients require bone grafting in specific areas before implants can be placed. Others have sufficient bone for immediate placement. The consultation includes a thorough review of your imaging, dental history, medical history, and what the process will realistically involve for your specific case.

Failing Dentition

Patients with multiple teeth that cannot be individually restored and require full-arch extraction are strong candidates for same-phase implant placement.

Denture Dissatisfaction

Current denture wearers who experience poor fit, instability, or difficulty eating and speaking are frequently excellent candidates for implant-supported full-arch restoration.

Significant Bone Loss

Patients with significant bone resorption may still be candidates using angled implant placement to engage available bone volume, sometimes avoiding the need for extensive grafting.

Edentulous Patients

Patients who are already fully edentulous in one or both arches can proceed directly to implant evaluation without extraction planning.


## The Full-Arch Implant Process at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


Full-arch restoration is a staged process, and understanding the timeline is important before you begin. In the surgical phase, any remaining failing teeth in the arch are extracted and four to six implants are placed. A temporary prosthesis is delivered on the same day or shortly after, allowing you to function with teeth during the healing period. This is where the “Teeth in a Day” description originates. The final, permanent prosthesis is fabricated after osseointegration is confirmed, typically several months later.

During the healing phase, patients follow a modified diet that avoids hard or chewy foods that could stress the implants before full integration. Our team provides detailed post-operative care instructions and monitoring appointments throughout the process. IV sedation or general anesthesia is used for the surgical phase to ensure patient comfort throughout what is a comprehensive procedure.

Comprehensive Evaluation

Full-arch 3D imaging, bone assessment, dental and medical history review, and candidacy determination. A clear timeline and cost estimate are provided.

Surgical Day

Extractions, implant placement, and temporary prosthesis delivery under IV sedation or general anesthesia. The surgical phase is completed in a single appointment.

Healing Phase

Osseointegration takes three to six months. You function on the temporary prosthesis during this period with a modified diet and scheduled follow-up appointments.

Final Prosthesis

After osseointegration is confirmed, the permanent prosthesis is fabricated and placed by your restorative provider, completing the full-arch restoration.


## Financing Full-Arch Restoration near West Los Angeles


Full-arch implant restoration is a significant investment, and we are transparent about costs from the beginning of the process. The total treatment cost depends on whether extractions are required, how many implants are placed, and whether bone grafting is needed. PPO dental insurance may provide partial coverage for certain components of the treatment, particularly extractions. We verify your benefits and provide a complete, itemized estimate at your consultation.

For the portions not covered by insurance, we offer flexible payment options through CareCredit, Alphaeon, and Cherry, all of which offer extended payment plans for high-value procedures. Visit our insurance and financing page for more detail on how we approach billing and financing for full-arch implant cases.


## Our Surgeons — Complex Implant Expertise Serving West Los Angeles


Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi completed his undergraduate neuroscience degree at UCLA and earned his DDS from USC School of Dentistry, graduating on the Dean’s List with the John Ingle Research Award. Dr. Saman Vahedi is a Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons and completed his residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, serving as Chief Resident in 2013 and 2014. Full-arch implant restoration is among the most complex procedures in oral surgery, and our board-certified team brings hospital-trained precision to every case.


## Frequently Asked Questions — All-On-X Dental Implants near West Los Angeles


What is the difference between All-on-4 and All-on-X?

All-on-4 refers to a specific protocol using four implants to support a full-arch prosthesis. All-on-X is a broader term that encompasses variations using four, five, or six implants, depending on the patient’s bone volume and anatomy. The number of implants is determined based on your specific imaging and surgical plan, not a one-size-fits-all protocol.

Will I leave surgery with teeth?

In most cases, yes. A temporary fixed prosthesis is placed at the time of surgery or within a very short period afterward, allowing you to function with teeth during the osseointegration phase. This is what is meant by “Teeth in a Day.” The temporary prosthesis is later replaced with the final permanent prosthesis after healing is complete.

Is full-arch restoration the same as a denture?

No. A traditional full denture rests on the gum tissue and is removable. A full-arch implant restoration is fixed to titanium implants anchored in the bone. It does not shift, need adhesive, or come out for cleaning. It functions and feels significantly more like natural teeth than a removable denture.

How long does the full process take from consultation to final prosthesis?

The full process typically spans six to twelve months from consultation to final prosthesis delivery, depending on whether pre-surgical procedures such as bone grafting are needed and how quickly osseointegration progresses. We provide a realistic timeline at your consultation based on your specific imaging and treatment plan.

Can I finance full-arch implants?

Yes. We work with CareCredit, Alphaeon, and Cherry, all of which offer payment plans suited for high-value dental procedures. Extended low-interest or deferred-interest options are often available. We walk you through financing options at your consultation along with your insurance benefits verification and cost estimate.

What if I have been told I don’t have enough bone for implants?

Many patients who have been told they lack sufficient bone for implants are still candidates for full-arch restoration using angled implant placement techniques or bone grafting. We recommend a consultation and Cone Beam 3D imaging evaluation before accepting a general dentist’s conclusion that implants are not possible. The clinical picture is often more nuanced than a two-dimensional X-ray can reveal.

## Sedation Options for Brentwood Patients Who Need Comfort During Oral Surgery


Dental anxiety is one of the most common reasons patients delay care, and for many people in Brentwood, that delay compounds into a more complex problem by the time they finally come in. If you have been putting off a necessary oral surgery procedure because of fear, discomfort, or a difficult past experience, sedation may be the factor that changes everything. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326 just minutes from Brentwood, IV sedation and general anesthesia are administered by our board-certified surgeons, not a separate provider, making the experience streamlined, safe, and cost-effective.

Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center offers the full range of sedation options for oral surgery procedures, from local anesthesia for simple cases to deep IV sedation and general anesthesia for complex or anxiety-driven situations.


## Types of Sedation We Offer


Not every procedure or patient requires the same level of sedation. Our surgeons evaluate your medical history, anxiety level, and procedure complexity to recommend the right option for you. We discuss this thoroughly at your consultation so there are no surprises on the day of surgery.

Local Anesthesia

Numbs the surgical site only. You remain fully awake and aware. Appropriate for straightforward extractions and minor procedures.

Oral Sedation

A prescription medication taken before your appointment that reduces anxiety. You remain conscious but significantly more relaxed throughout the procedure.

IV Sedation

Administered intravenously by our board-certified surgeons. You are deeply relaxed with no memory of the procedure. The most common choice for wisdom teeth and implant surgery.

General Anesthesia

Full unconsciousness for more complex surgical cases or patients with significant medical or behavioral factors. Administered in-office by our credentialed team.


## Why Surgeon-Administered Sedation Matters


Many patients do not realize that the person administering sedation varies widely between dental and surgical offices. At some practices, sedation is handled by a separate anesthesiologist brought in from outside, adding cost and coordination complexity. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, IV sedation and general anesthesia are administered directly by Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi. Both surgeons completed hospital-based oral and maxillofacial surgery residencies where surgical sedation was a core competency, and both hold the required anesthesia permits issued by the state of California.

This matters for Brentwood patients because it means you are never dealing with a separate scheduling chain, a second provider who does not know your case, or additional facility fees for sedation services. Everything is coordinated by the same team that performs your surgery.


## Procedures Commonly Performed Under Sedation


While sedation is available for any procedure when clinically appropriate, the most common cases at our practice where patients choose IV sedation or general anesthesia include the following. Each of these procedures is performed by our board-certified surgeons with precise pre-operative planning using our in-house Cone Beam 3D imaging technology.

The most common procedure performed under IV sedation. Most patients have no memory of the surgery and recover comfortably at home the same day. Learn about wisdom tooth extractions.

Dental Implant Surgery

For patients placing multiple implants or undergoing simultaneous bone grafting, IV sedation is frequently the right choice for comfort and procedural efficiency.

Patients undergoing bone grafting prior to implant placement often prefer IV sedation, particularly for larger grafts involving multiple sites.

Impacted Teeth

Removal of impacted canines or other teeth often involves more complex surgical access, making sedation the preferred option for patient comfort and surgical precision.


## What to Expect Before, During, and After Sedation


Sedation requires advance preparation. You will need to follow specific pre-anesthesia instructions provided at your consultation, which typically include fasting for a set period before surgery and stopping certain medications. On the day of surgery, a responsible adult must drive you to and from our office and stay with you for the first few hours of recovery. Do not plan to drive, operate machinery, or make significant decisions for the remainder of the day after IV sedation.

Most patients wake from IV sedation feeling calm and comfortable. Some experience mild grogginess or nausea in the first hour, which typically resolves quickly. We provide complete post-operative care instructions before you leave and remain available for follow-up questions during your recovery. Our team can also walk you through what to expect over the phone if you have concerns before your appointment.


## Insurance and Payment for Sedation Services


Coverage for sedation varies by procedure and insurance plan. When sedation is medically necessary, such as for impacted wisdom teeth or complex surgical extractions, many PPO dental plans provide at least partial coverage. For elective sedation or procedures where anesthesia is comfort-based rather than medical, coverage is less predictable. We verify your benefits before your procedure and provide a clear estimate of out-of-pocket costs. Review our insurance and financing page for more detail, and visit our payment options page to learn about CareCredit, Alphaeon, and Cherry financing.


## Our Surgeons — Sedation Administered by Board-Certified Oral Surgeons


At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, sedation is never delegated to an outside provider. Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi, who completed his undergraduate neuroscience degree at UCLA and his DDS at USC School of Dentistry, and Dr. Saman Vahedi, a Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons who completed his residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, both hold California anesthesia permits and have administered hundreds of sedation cases in hospital and office-based settings. Your safety and comfort are managed by the same hands performing your surgery.


## Frequently Asked Questions — Sedation Dentistry near Brentwood


Will I be completely unconscious under IV sedation?

IV sedation produces a deeply relaxed state where most patients have no memory of the procedure, but it is technically not the same as general anesthesia, where you are fully unconscious. The distinction is clinical, not practical for most patients. If full unconsciousness is required for your case, general anesthesia is also available.

Can I request sedation even if my procedure is straightforward?

Yes. Dental anxiety is a valid medical consideration, and we take it seriously. If you have significant anxiety about oral surgery regardless of procedure complexity, we will discuss sedation options during your consultation and determine the safest and most appropriate level for your situation.

Who administers the sedation at your practice?

Sedation is administered directly by Dr. Shadi or Dr. Vahedi, both board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons with California anesthesia permits and hospital-based residency training in surgical sedation. We do not use outside anesthesiologists for in-office procedures.

How long does IV sedation last after the procedure?

The sedative effects typically begin to wear off within one to two hours of your procedure ending, but residual drowsiness, impaired judgment, and slowed reflexes can persist for the remainder of the day. You should not drive, use machinery, or make important decisions until the following day.

Do I need to fast before IV sedation?

Yes. You will receive specific pre-anesthesia instructions at your consultation, which typically include fasting from solid food for a minimum period before surgery. Following these instructions exactly is important for your safety. We will walk you through all requirements well before your appointment date.

Is sedation covered by insurance?

Coverage depends on your specific plan and whether the sedation is deemed medically necessary. When sedation accompanies a covered surgical procedure such as impacted wisdom teeth removal, many PPO plans cover at least a portion. We verify your benefits before your appointment and provide a full cost estimate so there are no surprises.

## In-Office Sedation for Santa Monica Patients — Administered by Your Surgeon, Not a Separate Provider


Many oral surgery practices in and around Santa Monica refer patients to a hospital or ambulatory surgery center when sedation is needed, adding cost, scheduling complexity, and unfamiliar providers to an already stressful situation. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326 just east of Santa Monica, IV sedation and general anesthesia are administered in-office by Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi, the same board-certified surgeons who perform your procedure. The result is a more streamlined, consistent experience without the overhead of a hospital or surgery center visit.

Santa Monica patients include a broad cross-section of working professionals, families, bilingual households, and individuals who prioritize access and efficiency in their healthcare decisions. Our practice is designed to serve that patient base well. We offer sedation across all of our oral surgery procedures, including wisdom teeth removal, dental implants, bone grafting, and impacted tooth exposure.


## The Advantage of In-Office Sedation for Santa Monica Patients


When sedation is administered in a dedicated oral surgery practice rather than a hospital, several things change in your favor. You work with a single team from consultation through recovery. Your surgeon knows your medical history and planned procedure before the first dose is administered. Scheduling is managed through one office, with one set of pre-operative instructions, and one recovery plan. There are no separate facility fees for an external surgery center.

This is not a minor point for Santa Monica patients managing busy schedules. Hospital-based sedation appointments often involve separate pre-admission appointments, facility check-ins, and post-operative monitoring by nursing staff who have no context about the oral procedure that was just completed. In-office sedation at a surgical practice keeps all of that within one experienced team.

One Team, One Appointment

Your surgeon administers your sedation and performs your procedure. No coordination between separate providers or facilities.

No Hospital Overhead

In-office sedation avoids the facility fees, separate anesthesiologist billing, and extended scheduling timelines that come with hospital-based care.

Full Sedation Depth Available

We offer the complete range from local anesthesia through deep IV sedation and general anesthesia, selected based on your case and comfort level.

Bilingual Team

Our team communicates in English, Spanish, and Farsi/Persian, ensuring clear pre- and post-operative communication for Santa Monica’s diverse patient population.


## Procedures Available With Sedation


We offer IV sedation and general anesthesia for a wide range of oral surgery procedures. Most patients who choose sedation experience no memory of the procedure and recover comfortably at home the same day. A responsible adult must drive you home and stay with you for the first few hours after any sedation appointment.

The procedures most commonly performed under IV sedation at our practice include wisdom teeth removal, single and multiple implant placement, bone grafting, exposure of impacted canines and other impacted teeth, and surgical extractions involving complex root anatomy. For each case, sedation level is determined based on procedure complexity, patient anxiety, and medical history, and is discussed thoroughly at your pre-operative consultation. Review our pre-operative guidelines and pre-anesthesia instructions for more detail on what to expect.


## Insurance and Costs for Sedation near Santa Monica


Coverage for sedation depends on your plan and whether the anesthesia is considered medically necessary given the procedure being performed. For impacted wisdom teeth and complex surgical cases, many PPO dental plans cover at least a portion of the sedation fee. For elective sedation in lower-complexity cases, coverage is more variable. Our front office team verifies your specific benefits before your appointment and provides a full cost estimate, so you know exactly what to expect before you commit.

For costs beyond insurance coverage, we offer flexible payment options through third-party financing. Visit our insurance and financing page for an overview of accepted plans and financing options available to Santa Monica patients.


## Our Surgeons — California-Permitted Sedation Providers Serving Santa Monica


Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi holds a neuroscience degree from UCLA and his DDS from USC School of Dentistry, where he graduated on the Dean’s List and received the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. Dr. Saman Vahedi, a Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, completed his residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center and served as Chief Resident in 2013 and 2014. Both surgeons hold the California permits required to administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in an office setting.


## Frequently Asked Questions — Sedation Dentistry near Santa Monica


Is in-office sedation as safe as hospital sedation?

For the procedures performed at our practice, in-office sedation administered by board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons with California anesthesia permits is well within the scope of established clinical standards. Our surgeons trained in hospital-based residency programs where surgical sedation was a core competency. The setting is different from a hospital operating room, but the clinical preparation and monitoring are rigorous.

Do you offer sedation in Spanish or Farsi?

Yes. Our team communicates in English, Spanish, and Farsi/Persian. Pre-operative sedation instructions, consent discussions, and post-operative follow-up can all be conducted in your preferred language. We understand that clear communication before and after sedation is critical to a safe experience.

What sedation options are available for my procedure?

We offer local anesthesia for straightforward cases, IV sedation for most oral surgery procedures, and general anesthesia when clinically appropriate. The right option depends on your procedure complexity, medical history, and anxiety level, and is determined collaboratively with you at your consultation.

Do I need someone to drive me home after sedation?

Yes, a responsible adult must drive you home and remain with you for the first few hours after IV sedation or general anesthesia. You cannot take a rideshare alone. Do not plan to drive, operate machinery, or make significant decisions for the rest of the day following your sedation appointment.

Does my dental insurance cover sedation?

Coverage varies by procedure and plan. When sedation is medically necessary for a covered procedure such as impacted wisdom teeth removal, many PPO plans provide at least partial coverage. We verify your specific benefits before your appointment and walk you through your expected costs before any treatment begins.

How do I prepare for sedation surgery?

We provide detailed pre-anesthesia instructions at your consultation. In general, you will be required to fast for a specified period before surgery and may need to pause certain medications. Read through these instructions carefully and contact us before your appointment if you have any questions about preparation.

Sedation should not be an obstacle to getting the oral surgery you need. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, our board-certified surgeons handle sedation directly, making the experience simpler and more integrated than a hospital or separate surgery center visit. We are minutes from Santa Monica and ready to help you move forward with confidence.

Request your appointment online or reach out through our contact page. We serve patients from across the Westside, including Santa Monica, West Los Angeles, and Westwood. View all the communities we serve on the Westside.

## Oral Surgery With Sedation for Westwood Patients — Administered by Your Surgeon


Many Westwood patients, including graduate students, pre-med and dental students, and research faculty who understand healthcare inside and out, still find themselves anxious about oral surgery. Understanding a procedure intellectually and being comfortable going through it are different experiences. If anxiety, a difficult past dental experience, or the complexity of your procedure has led you to defer necessary care, sedation may be the piece that changes the equation. Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, located at 12300 Wilshire Blvd #326 just east of Westwood, offers IV sedation and general anesthesia administered directly by our board-certified surgeons, not a separate anesthesiologist, keeping the experience streamlined and integrated.

Our practice serves Westwood patients who want qualified, evidence-based care in a setting designed for professionals and students with high expectations and busy schedules.


## Sedation Options We Offer


We offer a full range of sedation options, from local anesthesia for straightforward cases to IV sedation and general anesthesia for more complex procedures or patients with significant anxiety. Sedation level is selected based on your procedure, medical history, and preference, and is discussed in detail at your consultation so you know exactly what to expect.

Local Anesthesia

Numbs the surgical site. You remain fully awake. Used for straightforward extractions and procedures where anxiety is not a significant factor.

Nitrous Oxide

A mild sedative inhaled through a nasal mask that reduces anxiety while keeping you conscious. Effects wear off quickly after the procedure ends.

IV Sedation

Delivered intravenously by our board-certified surgeons. Deep relaxation with no memory of the procedure. The most common choice for wisdom teeth and implant surgery.

General Anesthesia

Full unconsciousness for highly complex cases or patients with significant behavioral or medical factors. Administered in-office by our permited surgeons.


## Why In-Office Sedation at an Oral Surgery Practice Makes Sense


For Westwood and UCLA community members who have done their research, the distinction between in-office sedation administered by an oral surgeon and hospital-based sedation managed by a separate anesthesiologist is a meaningful one. When your oral surgeon administers the sedation, there is no coordination between two separate providers who have not discussed your case together. The surgeon knows your imaging, your procedure plan, your medical history, and your anxiety level. The sedation is calibrated to that specific context.

Hospital or ambulatory surgery center sedation involves additional scheduling, facility fees, and provider coordination that adds complexity and cost without adding clinical benefit for the types of procedures we perform. Our surgeons, Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi, hold California anesthesia permits and completed their training in hospital-based residency programs where in-office surgical sedation was a core clinical competency. You can review the evidence base for in-office oral surgery sedation through resources like the National Library of Medicine, which documents the clinical foundations of contemporary oral surgery practice.


## What Sedation Feels Like and What to Expect


For patients who have never experienced IV sedation, understanding what it actually involves can reduce pre-procedure anxiety. Most patients describe the onset of IV sedation as a rapid deepening relaxation within seconds of the medication being administered. Surgery proceeds, and most patients retain no memory of the procedure at all. Waking up feels like coming out of a light sleep. Some patients experience mild grogginess, nausea, or emotional lability in the first hour post-procedure, all of which resolve quickly.

Preparation is important. You will receive specific pre-anesthesia instructions covering fasting requirements and medication adjustments before your procedure. A responsible adult must drive you home and stay with you for the first few hours. You should not drive, operate machinery, or make significant decisions on the day of your sedation appointment. We also provide detailed post-operative care instructions and remain available for any questions that come up during recovery.


## Insurance and Cost for Sedation near Westwood


When sedation is medically necessary, such as for impacted wisdom teeth or complex surgical procedures, many PPO dental plans provide at least partial coverage. UCLA students on UC SHIP and employees with UC Benefits dental coverage should verify sedation benefits prior to their appointment, which we do on your behalf. For elective sedation in lower-complexity cases, out-of-pocket costs may apply. We provide a full breakdown before any procedure begins. Visit our payment options page and insurance and financing page for more information.


## Our Surgeons — Credentialed, California-Permitted, and Rooted in the Westwood Community


Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi completed his neuroscience degree at UCLA and his DDS from the USC School of Dentistry, where he earned Dean’s List recognition and the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. Dr. Saman Vahedi is a Diplomate of the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons and completed his hospital-based residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center. Both surgeons hold the California permits required to administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in an office setting and bring hospital-trained expertise to every sedated procedure.


## Frequently Asked Questions — Sedation Dentistry near Westwood


I’m a medical or dental student — is IV sedation still appropriate for me?

Absolutely. Clinical knowledge does not eliminate anxiety. Many healthcare students and professionals find that their familiarity with procedures actually heightens anticipatory anxiety because they can visualize what is happening in detail. IV sedation is appropriate based on clinical factors, not on your professional background. If your case and health status make you a good candidate, sedation is available regardless of your field.

Will I be monitored during IV sedation?

Yes. Throughout your sedated procedure, our team monitors your vital signs including blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation continuously. The equipment and protocols we use in-office are aligned with the standards required by California anesthesia permits for office-based oral surgery sedation.

Do I need to fast before IV sedation?

Yes. You will receive specific fasting instructions at your consultation, typically requiring you to avoid solid food for a minimum number of hours before surgery. Following these instructions exactly is essential for your safety. Contact us before your appointment if you have any questions about the requirements.

How long after sedation can I return to studying?

We recommend the full day of your procedure be reserved for rest. The sedative effects and residual medication can impair focus, memory consolidation, and judgment for the remainder of that day. Light reading or review work is generally possible by the following morning, though this depends on your procedure and the medications involved.

What if I have a health condition that affects sedation candidacy?

We review your full medical history before any sedation procedure. Certain conditions require special consideration, medication adjustments, or coordination with your primary care provider. We do this routinely and will let you know if your health profile requires additional preparation or if a modified sedation plan is more appropriate for your situation.

Is sedation available for all oral surgery procedures at your practice?

IV sedation is available for any procedure where it is clinically appropriate, including wisdom teeth removal, dental implant placement, bone grafting, and exposure of impacted teeth. Sedation level is determined by procedure complexity, patient health, and patient preference. Local anesthesia alone is used for some simpler cases where sedation adds little clinical value.

We are a short drive east on Wilshire Boulevard and committed to the kind of thorough, individualized care that the Westwood community expects.

# Dr. Saman Vahedi



### About Dr. Saman Vahedi


← Meet Our Team

Education

B.S. Molecular, Cell & Developmental Biology

UCLA

Dental School

DDS, Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry

USC

Residency

OMFS Residency, Univ. of Nebraska Medical Center

Chief Resident, 2013–2014

Board Certification

Diplomate, American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (ABOMS)

Dr. Saman Vahedi earned his B.S. in Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology from UCLA before continuing to the Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry of USC for his DDS. He then pursued one of the most rigorous training paths available in oral surgery: a hospital-based OMFS residency at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in Omaha. UNMC is an academic medical center where residents train alongside emergency medicine, trauma surgery, and internal medicine teams, handling cases that range from facial fractures arriving in the emergency department to complex elective jaw surgery and oral pathology.

Dr. Vahedi served as Chief Resident from 2013 to 2014, a position that reflects both clinical performance and leadership among a residency cohort. Following the completion of his residency, he went on to earn his Diplomate status from the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons. ABOMS board certification requires passing both a written qualifying examination and an oral certifying examination administered by a panel of credentialed surgeons, in addition to verified residency training and ongoing continuing education. It is the highest credential in the specialty, and fewer than half of practicing oral surgeons hold it.

Dr. Vahedi’s clinical scope at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center covers the full range of oral and maxillofacial surgery. He has extensive experience in facial trauma and fracture repair, orthognathic jaw surgery, oral pathology evaluation and biopsies, wisdom teeth extractions, IV general anesthesia, complex dental implant surgery, and bone grafting and ridge augmentation. His training at UNMC means that cases involving anatomical complexity, bone loss, sedation management, or any combination of procedures in a single visit fall squarely within what he is trained to handle.

What that level of training means in practice is a surgeon who approaches uncertainty and complexity without needing to refer out. Patients who have been told their case is “too complicated” at a general dental office or who need a combination of bone grafting, implant placement, and sedation managed together will find that Dr. Vahedi is prepared for those cases. You can also learn about his colleague, Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi, who shares the same commitment to rigorous, patient-centered care at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center.

### About Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi

Clinical Focus

Dental Implants • Wisdom Teeth

IV Anesthesia • Bone Grafting

Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi grew up in the West Los Angeles area, which makes Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center more than a practice location for him. After earning his B.S. in Neuroscience from UCLA with College Honors, he attended the University of Southern California School of Dentistry, where he made the Dean’s List multiple times and received the John Ingle Research Award in 2009. That award recognized his contributions to dental research as a student, a distinction that reflects the analytical approach he brings to clinical work today.

Following dental school, Dr. Shadi completed an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Internship at the Veterans’ Affairs Hospital in Long Beach before entering the full OMFS residency program at the University of California San Francisco–Fresno, completing in 2014. The UCSF–Fresno program trains surgeons across the full scope of oral and maxillofacial surgery, with significant exposure to trauma cases, reconstructive procedures, and complex anesthesia management. That training base is what qualifies Dr. Shadi to administer IV sedation and general anesthesia in-office, a capability that most general dental practices cannot offer.

Since completing his residency, Dr. Shadi has practiced in the Greater Los Angeles area, returning to the Westside community where he spent his formative years. His clinical focus centers on single and complex dental implant surgery, wisdom teeth extractions, bone grafting and ridge augmentation, and IV general anesthesia. Patients whose cases involve significant bone loss, impaction, or the need for sedation will find that Dr. Shadi’s training makes him well suited to handle them without outside referrals.

His background in neuroscience gives Dr. Shadi a particular attentiveness to the anxiety and comfort concerns that accompany oral surgery for many patients. Procedures that involve sedation or surgical complexity are also procedures that require clear communication and unhurried pre-operative conversation. That is what patients consistently describe in their experience with Dr. Shadi at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center. You can also learn more about his colleague, Dr. Saman Vahedi, whose board certification and academic medical center residency training complement Dr. Shadi’s approach at the practice.
