### The All-on-4 Dental Procedure: Step-by-Step Process Explained


Losing teeth can affect your daily life. It makes you feel shy about smiling. Simple tasks like eating become difficult ordeals. Yet, those old-fashioned dentures do not cut it. They lack stability and security. However, there is an excellent permanent solution called dental implants. It is revolutionary. The All-on-4 procedure allows doctors to replace your entire upper or lower set of teeth. Four implants are all it takes to anchor an entire arch of beautiful new teeth. This technique restores stunning, natural smiles that function well. You can grin with pride and eat whatever you want again. Imagine how that would transform your life. This dental implant procedure makes it possible.


### Hidden Benefits of Dental Implants: Things You Should Know


Are you on the fence about dental implants? When you lose a tooth, it's difficult to know how to handle the next steps. With other options like dentures or bridgework available, you may be wondering: why implants? Most people know dental implants as a more expensive cosmetic option, but they actually have hidden advantages that can make a higher upfront cost worthwhile. Let’s dig into some of the hidden benefits of dental implants:


### Care for Your Dental Implants With Wilshire Oral Surgery


So you got new dental implants! With a little attention to your dental health, implants can last a lifetime. Dental implants are a popular solution for replacing missing teeth, and for good reason. They can last a lifetime with proper care, and can be easier to upkeep than dentures. In this article, we'll review caring for your implants immediately after surgery, avoiding dental implant failure, and simple care and maintenance.


### Benefits of Dental Cone Beam CT: Cone Beam Computed Tomography & Imaging in Los Angeles


3D imaging is a relatively new dentistry practice. In years past, diagnostic processes used medical grade CTs or "CAT" scans to create clear imaging. 3D imaging allows dentists to plan for dental treatments like orthodontics or dental implants. Here, we'll dig into what dental cone beam computed tomography imaging (or CBCT) provides, and how treatment planning can benefit from it.


### PRF: Platelet Rich Fibrin in Dentistry at Wilshire Oral Surgery


Healthcare professionals are now elevating existing parts of the body's healing process to assist recovery and immunity. We're now able to harvest valuable growth factors to regrow tissue, re-inject blood after blood loss, and even augment our immune system to fight off disease. This is done by concentrating our existing growth factors and reintroducing them to the body in order to speed up the healing process. This may sound like magic, but it's just great use of the existing resources our bodies provide. One of the ways our body's wound healing process is now elevated is in the use of platelet-rich fibrin, a relatively new procedure with a variety of clinical applications.

# The Benefits of Corrective Jaw Surgery for Your Health and Appearance


Corrective jaw surgery, also known as orthognathic surgery, is a transformative procedure that addresses various functional and aesthetic concerns caused by jaw misalignment. Whether the issue stems from genetics, trauma, or developmental abnormalities, orthognathic surgery can provide life-changing benefits for both your health and appearance. Here’s a closer look at the advantages of this procedure and how it can improve your quality of life.


## Enhanced Jaw Function


Misaligned jaws can lead to difficulties in chewing, speaking, and even breathing. Corrective jaw surgery realigns the upper and lower jaws to improve functionality, enabling smoother, pain-free movements. This can help you enjoy your favorite meals and communicate with confidence.


### Relief from Jaw Pain and Disorders


Jaw misalignment often contributes to chronic conditions like temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders, which cause pain and discomfort in the jaw, neck, and shoulders. By correcting the jaw’s structure, orthognathic surgery can significantly reduce or eliminate these symptoms, restoring comfort and mobility.


### Improved Breathing and Sleep Quality


Conditions like sleep apnea are frequently linked to structural jaw issues. Orthognathic surgery can open up the airway, improving breathing patterns and reducing the severity of sleep apnea. Better sleep quality translates to increased energy, improved focus, and enhanced overall health.


### Enhanced Aesthetics


Corrective jaw surgery can reshape your face, harmonizing your features and enhancing your overall appearance. It addresses concerns such as:

A protruding or receding jaw

Facial asymmetry

An open bite or crossbite

The improved facial structure often boosts self-esteem and confidence.


### Long-Term Oral Health


Misaligned jaws can place undue stress on your teeth, leading to uneven wear, gum disease, and tooth decay. By aligning the jaw correctly, orthognathic surgery promotes better oral hygiene and reduces the risk of long-term dental problems.


### Speech Improvements


Jaw misalignment can impact speech clarity, making certain sounds difficult to pronounce. Post-surgery, many patients experience improved articulation and clarity, enhancing their ability to communicate effectively.


### Who Is a Candidate for Corrective Jaw Surgery?


Orthognathic surgery is often recommended for individuals with:

Severe jaw misalignment that cannot be corrected with orthodontics alone

Chronic jaw pain or TMJ disorders

Difficulty chewing, biting, or swallowing

Breathing or sleep-related issues caused by jaw structure

Facial asymmetry or disproportionate jaw growth


### Transform Your Health and Appearance


Corrective jaw surgery offers a life-changing solution for those struggling with jaw misalignment, enhancing both your health and appearance. From initial consultation to post-surgery recovery, our team is here to guide you every step of the way.

# Understanding Jaw Surgery: When Is It Necessary and What to Expect During Recovery


In the realm of oral and maxillofacial surgery, jaw surgery, also known as orthognathic surgery, stands as a transformative procedure that addresses a wide range of functional and aesthetic concerns. This intricate surgical intervention aims to correct misalignments of the jaws, creating a harmonious balance between the upper and lower jaws, and enhancing both the appearance and functionality of the bite.


## Understanding Orthognathic Surgery


Orthognathic surgery is a surgical procedure that involves repositioning one or both jaws to correct functional and aesthetic issues related to jaw misalignment or skeletal deformities. This procedure is often performed in conjunction with orthodontic treatment, creating a comprehensive approach to achieving optimal jaw alignment and a harmonious bite.

The primary goals of orthognathic surgery include:

Correcting skeletal discrepancies and malocclusions (misaligned bites)

Improving facial symmetry and aesthetics

Enhancing the ability to chew, speak, and breathe properly

Alleviating associated health issues, such as temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders or sleep apnea

By addressing these concerns, orthognathic surgery not only enhances the appearance of the face but also improves overall oral health and quality of life.


### When Jaw Surgery May Be Necessary


While jaw surgery may seem like a drastic measure, there are specific circumstances in which it becomes a necessary and highly recommended treatment option. These indications typically arise when routine orthodontic treatment alone cannot sufficiently address the underlying skeletal issues or severe malocclusions. Some common scenarios where jaw surgery may be indicated include:

Severe Underbite or Overbite: When the upper and lower jaws are significantly misaligned, resulting in an excessive protrusion or retrusion of the jaw(s), jaw surgery can correct this skeletal discrepancy.

Jaw Deformities: Congenital or acquired jaw deformities, such as cleft lip and palate, facial trauma, or developmental abnormalities, may require surgical intervention to restore proper jaw alignment and function.

Sleep Apnea: In cases where sleep apnea is caused by structural abnormalities in the jaw or airway, orthognathic surgery can be an effective treatment option by repositioning the jaws and improving airway patency.

Temporomandibular Joint (TMJ) Disorders: Certain TMJ disorders, such as chronic pain or jaw dysfunction, can be alleviated by correcting the underlying jaw misalignment through orthognathic surgery.

Facial Asymmetry: Significant facial asymmetry caused by jaw misalignment can be addressed through orthognathic surgery, improving both aesthetics and function.


### The Jaw Surgery Procedure


Orthognathic surgery is a complex procedure that involves repositioning one or both jaws to achieve optimal alignment and functional occlusion. The specific surgical approach and techniques used will depend on the individual case and the extent of correction required. However, the general process typically involves the following steps:

Anesthesia: The surgery is performed under general anesthesia, ensuring that you remain comfortable and pain-free throughout the procedure.

Surgical Incisions: Incisions are made inside the mouth, typically along the gum line, to access the underlying jawbones. In some cases, additional incisions may be made on the outside of the face, depending on the complexity of the case.

Bone Repositioning: Using specialized surgical tools and guided by detailed surgical planning, the surgeon will carefully reposition the jawbones to their desired positions. This may involve cutting and repositioning the jawbones, as well as securing them in place with plates, screws, or wires.

Bite Adjustment: Once the jaws are repositioned, the surgeon will carefully adjust the bite to ensure proper occlusion and alignment of the teeth.

Closure and Stabilization: The surgical incisions are closed with sutures or dissolvable stitches, and the jaws may be temporarily stabilized with elastic bands or other appliances to aid in the healing process.

The duration of the surgery can vary significantly, ranging from several hours to an entire day, depending on the complexity of the case and the extent of the corrections required.


### What to Expect During Recovery from Jaw Surgery


The recovery process following orthognathic surgery is a crucial phase that requires patience, diligence, and adherence to your surgeon’s instructions. While the initial weeks can be challenging, it is essential to prioritize your recovery to ensure optimal healing and long-term success. Here’s what you can expect during the recovery period:

Initial Discomfort and Swelling: In the immediate post-operative period, you may experience some discomfort, swelling, and bruising around the surgical site. Your surgeon will prescribe appropriate pain medication and provide instructions for managing these temporary side effects.

Dietary Restrictions: For the first few weeks following surgery, you will be restricted to a liquid or soft food diet to allow the surgical site to heal properly. Gradually, you will be able to transition to a more solid diet as directed by your healthcare team.

Oral Hygiene Considerations: Maintaining excellent oral hygiene is crucial during the recovery process. Your surgical team will provide specific instructions on how to clean your mouth and care for the surgical site properly.

Follow-up Appointments: Regular follow-up appointments with your surgeon and orthodontist are essential to monitor your progress and make any necessary adjustments to your treatment plan.

While the recovery timeline can vary based on the individual case, most patients can expect to experience significant improvements in their bite, facial appearance, and overall oral function within several months after the surgery. It is important to follow your surgeon’s instructions closely and remain patient throughout the recovery process to achieve the best possible outcome.


### Embracing the Journey to a Better Smile


Jaw surgery is a transformative procedure that can have a profound impact on an individual’s life. While the journey may be challenging, the rewards of improved oral function, enhanced facial aesthetics, and a boost in self-confidence make it a worthwhile investment.

Throughout the process, it is essential to maintain open communication with your healthcare team, follow their instructions diligently, and embrace the recovery period with patience and determination. By doing so, you can increase your chances of achieving optimal results and embarking on a new chapter with a beautiful, functional, and confident smile.

If you or someone you know is considering jaw surgery, schedule a consultation with our experienced team of oral and maxillofacial surgeons. Our dedicated professionals will guide you through every step of the process, answering your questions, addressing your concerns, and providing personalized care tailored to your unique needs. Visit Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center at our office in Los Angeles, California, or call (310) 954-9449 to book an appointment today.

# Your Guide to Tooth Extraction: What to Expect Before, During, and After


Tooth extraction is a common dental procedure that involves the removal of a tooth from its socket in the jawbone. While it may sound daunting, tooth extraction is often necessary to maintain oral health and prevent further complications.


## Reasons Why Tooth Extraction May Be Necessary


There are several reasons why a tooth extraction may be necessary. One of the most common reasons is severe tooth decay or damage that cannot be repaired by other dental treatments such as fillings or crowns.

In some cases, a tooth may also need to be extracted if it poses a threat to the surrounding teeth or if it is causing overcrowding in the mouth. Additionally, impacted wisdom teeth, which are third molars that do not have enough space to erupt properly, often require extraction to prevent pain, infection, and other complications.


### Preparing for a Tooth Extraction


Before a tooth extraction, your surgeon will perform a thorough examination of your mouth and take X-rays to assess the condition of the tooth and surrounding structures. They will also review your medical history to ensure that you are a suitable candidate for the procedure. It is important to inform your doctor about any medications you are taking, as well as any medical conditions or allergies you have. Based on their evaluation, your doctor will discuss the treatment plan with you, including the type of anesthesia that will be used during the extraction.


### What to Expect During a Tooth Extraction Procedure


On the day of the tooth extraction, your surgeon will numb the area around the tooth with a local anesthetic to ensure that you do not feel any pain during the procedure. If you are having multiple teeth extracted or if the tooth is impacted, your surgeon may recommend general anesthesia or conscious sedation to keep you comfortable throughout the procedure.

Once the area is numb, your surgeon will carefully loosen the tooth using a dental instrument called an elevator. They will then use forceps to gently remove the tooth from its socket. In some cases, a tooth may need to be sectioned into smaller pieces for easier removal. The entire process is usually quick and relatively painless.


### Aftercare and Recovery Tips Following a Tooth Extraction


After a tooth extraction, it is important to follow your doctor’s aftercare instructions to ensure proper healing and minimize the risk of complications. Immediately after the procedure, your surgeon will provide you with gauze pads to bite down on to control bleeding. It is normal to experience some swelling and discomfort in the first few days following the extraction. Applying an ice pack to the affected area for 15 minutes at a time can help reduce swelling. You should also avoid drinking through a straw, smoking, and eating hard or sticky foods for at least 24 hours after the extraction. It is crucial to keep the extraction site clean by gently rinsing your mouth with warm saltwater. Your dentist may also prescribe pain medication or antibiotics if necessary.


### Schedule Your Consultation with Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


By understanding what to expect before, during, and after a tooth extraction, you can prepare yourself both physically and mentally for the procedure. Consult with your surgeon, follow their aftercare instructions, and reach out to them if you have any concerns or questions during the recovery process. Taking proper care of your mouth after a tooth extraction will help ensure a smooth and successful healing process.

If you have any questions or concerns about tooth extraction, schedule a consultation with our professionals at Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center in our Los Angeles, California, office. Please call (310) 954-9449 to book an appointment today.

# How Impacted Canine Teeth Can Disrupt Your Daily Life and Smile


Impacted canine teeth are more common than you might think, and if left untreated, they can cause more than just cosmetic concerns. For many people in Los Angeles, where a confident smile is everything, impacted canines can be a frustrating and sometimes painful issue.


## What Are Impacted Canine Teeth?


Your canine teeth—often called “eye teeth” or “fangs”—play a critical role in your bite. They help guide your other teeth into place, tear food, and support a strong, well-aligned jaw. However, sometimes these teeth don’t erupt as they should and instead remain trapped under the gums or stuck against other teeth.

Impacted canine often occurs due to lack of space in the mouth, genetic factors, or obstructions like baby teeth that never fell out properly. While it’s common for wisdom teeth to become impacted, canine teeth are unique because they’re essential for both function and aesthetics.


### How Impacted Canine Teeth Can Affect Your Daily Life


1. Changes to Your Smile and Confidence

In a city like Los Angeles, where first impressions and self-image can make all the difference, an impacted canine tooth can disrupt your smile’s natural alignment. A missing or out-of-place tooth can make people feel self-conscious, leading them to hide their smile in photos or social situations.

2. Difficulty Eating and Speaking

Canine teeth are essential for tearing food efficiently. If one is impacted, you may find yourself favoring one side of your mouth when chewing, leading to uneven wear on your teeth. Some people also experience speech difficulties, especially if the impacted tooth has caused crowding or misalignment.

3. Pain and Discomfort

Impacted canines don’t always hurt, but when they do, the discomfort can be persistent. You might feel pressure in your gums, experience tenderness around the jaw, or even develop cysts or infections if the tooth remains stuck for too long. If you’re dealing with jaw pain or unexplained soreness in your gums, an impacted canine could be the culprit.

4. Increased Risk of Dental Issues

When a canine tooth fails to erupt, it can create a domino effect of oral health problems. The pressure from an impacted tooth can cause damage to neighboring teeth, potentially leading to misalignment, enamel erosion, or even tooth loss over time. Additionally, food and bacteria can become trapped around the impacted area, increasing the risk of gum disease and cavities.


### What Can Be Done?


The good news is that impacted canines can be treated successfully with the right approach. Depending on the severity of the impaction and your age, treatment may involve:

• Surgical Exposure – If the tooth is stuck beneath the gums, a minor surgical procedure can help expose it so it can be guided into place.

• Tooth Extraction & Replacement – In severe cases, where the impacted tooth cannot be saved, it may need to be removed and replaced with a dental implant.


### Don’t Let an Impacted Canine Hold You Back


If you’re struggling with an impacted canine tooth, it’s not something to ignore. Early intervention can prevent long-term dental complications and help you achieve the healthy, confident smile you deserve. Whether you need a surgical procedure or guidance on your best treatment options, our team is here to help.

At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we specialize in diagnosing and treating impacted canine teeth with personalized, expert care. Visit our office in Los Angeles, California, or call (310) 954-9449 to schedule a consultation today.

# Is Socket Preservation Necessary for Everyone Who Has a Tooth Extracted?


When a tooth is extracted, the empty socket left behind can lead to changes in your jawbone over time. This is a natural part of the healing process, but it can also cause problems if you plan to replace the missing tooth with a dental implant or want to maintain your facial structure and oral health. One way to manage this change is through a procedure called socket preservation.


## What Is Socket Preservation?


Socket preservation is a technique used to minimize bone loss after a tooth is removed. After the extraction, a bone graft material is placed in the empty socket to help preserve the shape and volume of the bone. The area is usually covered with a protective membrane and sutured to encourage healing. This procedure helps keep the jawbone intact, making it easier to place a dental implant later and preventing the sunken appearance that can result from bone loss.


### Who Should Consider Socket Preservation?


Socket preservation is particularly beneficial for individuals who plan to get a dental implant in the future. It is also recommended for those who have thin or fragile jawbones, as maintaining bone volume is essential for future procedures and overall jaw health. Patients who are concerned about preserving the natural appearance of their facial structure may also benefit, as bone loss can lead to changes in facial contours over time.

Additionally, those with multiple missing teeth who are considering full or partial dentures may find socket preservation helpful in creating a stable foundation for their prosthetics. By preserving the bone structure, this treatment can significantly improve the success of future dental restorations and support long-term oral health.


### Is It Necessary for Everyone?


While socket preservation offers many advantages, it is not always necessary for every patient. In some cases, such as when the extracted tooth is located in the back of the mouth where aesthetics and implant placement are less of a concern, the procedure may not be needed. Patients who do not intend to replace the missing tooth may also choose to forgo socket preservation.

Additionally, if there is already significant bone loss or the presence of infection, other treatments may be prioritized first. Ultimately, the decision depends on each individual’s long-term dental goals, current oral health, and the specific circumstances surrounding the extraction site.


### Schedule a Consultation Today


Socket preservation is not required for everyone, but it can be an important step in protecting your long-term oral health, especially if you plan to restore the missing tooth. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we will assess your individual needs and goals to determine whether socket preservation is the right choice for you.

If you are facing a tooth extraction and wondering about the next steps, contact Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center to schedule a consultation and learn more about your treatment options. Visit our office in Los Angeles, California, or call (310) 954-9449 to book an appointment today.

# Post-Operative Care for Oral Surgery: What You Need to Know


Undergoing oral surgery can be a major step towards achieving better oral health and comfort. However, the success of your surgery doesn’t end in the operating room. Proper post-operative care is essential to ensure optimal healing, minimize discomfort, and prevent complications. Here’s a guide on what to expect after your procedure and how to take care of yourself in the crucial recovery period.


## Managing Discomfort and Swelling


After oral surgery, it’s normal to experience some swelling and discomfort. To manage these symptoms:

Apply Ice: Place an ice pack on the affected area in 15-minute intervals (15 minutes on, 15 minutes off) during the first 24 hours.

Take Pain Medication as Prescribed: Over-the-counter or prescribed pain relievers can help reduce discomfort. Avoid aspirin, as it can increase bleeding.

Elevate Your Head: Sleeping with your head elevated can reduce swelling and ease breathing.


### Controlling Bleeding


Minor bleeding is common after oral surgery, especially within the first few hours.

Use Gauze Pads: Place a gauze pad over the surgical site and bite down gently to apply pressure. Change the gauze every 30-45 minutes, or as advised by your oral surgeon.

Avoid Straws and Spitting: The suction motion can dislodge the blood clot, prolonging bleeding and potentially leading to dry socket—a painful condition that can delay healing.

Limit Physical Activity: Rest for the first 24-48 hours and avoid any strenuous activity that could increase blood pressure and cause bleeding.


### Dietary Considerations


Eating the right foods after oral surgery is important to avoid irritating the surgical site.

Start with Soft Foods: Soups, yogurts, smoothies, and mashed potatoes are gentle on your mouth. Gradually return to normal foods as you feel comfortable.

Avoid Hot and Spicy Foods: High temperatures and spices can irritate your mouth and delay healing.

Stay Hydrated: Drink plenty of water, but avoid carbonated or acidic beverages that could irritate the area.


### Maintaining Oral Hygiene


Keeping your mouth clean is crucial, but it must be done carefully.

Rinse Gently: Starting 24 hours after surgery, rinse your mouth with a warm saltwater solution (1 teaspoon of salt in 8 ounces of water) a few times a day, especially after meals.

Avoid Brushing Near the Surgical Site: Brush the rest of your teeth as usual, but be cautious around the surgical area to avoid disrupting the healing tissue.

Do Not Use Mouthwash: Many commercial mouthwashes contain alcohol, which can irritate the surgical site. Your oral surgeon may recommend a gentle rinse instead.


### Preventing Infection


Following the post-operative care instructions from your surgeon is vital for avoiding infections.

Take Prescribed Antibiotics: If antibiotics are prescribed, take them exactly as directed to prevent any infection.

Watch for Signs of Infection: Keep an eye out for signs such as increased swelling after the first few days, excessive pain, fever, or discharge from the surgical site. If any of these occur, contact your oral surgeon immediately.


### Avoiding Habits That Delay Healing


Certain habits can slow the healing process or cause complications:

Do Not Smoke or Use Tobacco Products: Smoking can significantly delay healing and increase the risk of dry socket.

Avoid Alcohol Consumption: Alcohol can interfere with medications and delay recovery. Wait until your surgeon gives the green light.


### When to Seek Help


While most discomfort and swelling should gradually subside, it’s essential to know when to reach out to your oral surgeon. Seek medical advice if:

You experience severe or worsening pain that doesn’t improve with medication.

You have prolonged bleeding that doesn’t subside after applying pressure.

You notice signs of infection or have a fever.


### Ensuring a Smooth & Successful Recovery


By following these post-operative care tips, you’re setting yourself up for a smooth and speedy recovery. At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, we are here to support you every step of the way.

Reach out to Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center if you have any questions or concerns about your post-operative care. Contact our office in Los Angeles, California, by calling (310) 954-9449 to book an appointment today.

# PRF: Platelet Rich Fibrin in Dentistry at Wilshire Oral Surgery


Healthcare professionals are now elevating existing parts of the body's healing process to assist recovery and immunity. We're now able to harvest valuable growth factors to regrow tissue, re-inject blood after blood loss, and even augment our immune system to fight off disease. This is done by concentrating our existing growth factors and reintroducing them to the body in order to speed up the healing process. This may sound like magic, but it's just great use of the existing resources our bodies provide. One of the ways our body's wound healing process is now elevated is in the use of platelet-rich fibrin, a relatively new procedure with a variety of clinical applications.

What is Platelet Rich Fibrin?

Platelet Rich Fibrin, or PRF, is a concentrated biomaterial that can speed up the healing process. PRF relies on blood platelets, which are known for their role in healing wounds. These growth factors can now be extracted and concentrated for medical use. When injected, PRF increases growth factors in areas of the body, promoting tissue regeneration.

PRF is a relatively new part of regenerative medicine and is considered a fresh alternative to platelet-rich plasma. In the PRF process, the blood is spun at a slower speed than PRP, allowing for the preservation of more stem cells and white blood cells. With this updated procedure, PRF allows for slower release of growth factors than PRP, continuing to benefit the body for 7-10 days.


### How does PRF work?


The PRF process begins with a minimally invasive draw of the patient’s blood. The blood is then placed in a centrifuge and spun at a specific speed to separate needed platelets and growth factors from the rest of the blood’s makeup. After blood has been separated into layers, the PRF layer is extremely rich in growth factors. After the RPF layer has been concentrated, the sample is ready for use at the surgical site.


### What are the benefits of platelet-rich fibrin?


PRF can be used to reduce healing times in surgery, promoting faster tissue or bone regeneration. It’s not just useful in dentistry! While it can be used in maxillofacial surgery, it has also been utilized in orthopedic, cardiovascular, facial rejuvenation, and even plastic surgery.

Use of PRF also allows us to avoid unnatural anti-coagulants or additives, relying solely on the body’s existing resources. This is helpful for patients who want faster bone and soft tissue regeneration without synthetic additives.


### What are the benefits of PRF in dentistry?


The applications of PRF in dentistry are incredibly helpful and wide-reaching. PRF can be highly effective in combating gum disease or recession. It is often injected after gum grafting surgery to regenerate healthy gum tissue. In oral surgery requiring bone grafting, PRF can assist with bone growth and density. PRF therapy is also commonly used during the dental implant process. When injected at the implant site, it can lead to faster healing, less postoperative pain, and an increased likelihood that the body will accept the implant. This is because the bone and tissue reintegrate faster, allowing for less time for complications. These are just some of the various applications for growth factors.


### How Does Wilshire Oral Surgery Use PRF?


PRF is a straightforward, widely used element of many dental procedures. At Wilshire Oral Surgery, PRF is used in many ways, including:

Improving healing time after extractions (including wisdom teeth/third molars)

Enhancing bone healing in preparation for implant placement

Boosting soft tissue or gum healing around teeth or implants

Use as sinus augmentation (sinus lift) material

If you’re interested in utilizing the many benefits of platelet-rich fibrin in your next dental procedure, contact Wilshire Oral Surgery.

# Hidden Benefits of Dental Implants: Things You Should Know


Are you on the fence about dental implants? When you lose a tooth, it's difficult to know how to handle the next steps. With other options like dentures or bridgework available, you may be wondering: why implants? Most people know dental implants as a more expensive cosmetic option, but they actually have hidden advantages that can make a higher upfront cost worthwhile. Let’s dig into some of the hidden benefits of dental implants:


## Dental Implants Don’t Need To Be That Painful


Going into any dental surgery, it’s normal to be wary about pain. However, dental implant surgery can cause minimal discomfort and do wonders for your oral health long term. People even return to work the day after getting implants! Your dentist will use local anesthesia, so you likely won’t feel pain during the surgery itself. Most patients report feeling pressure during surgery, but not pain. Many patients also opt for sedation during the surgery, and take over-the-counter pain relief or prescription medication after. Take your surgery as an opportunity to stock up on ice cream, pudding, and other fun foods to eat while you’re recovering. If implants are on the horizon for you, you can experience lower pain levels with proper preparation!


## Your Lifestyle Can Stay The Same After Getting Dental Implants


Unlike dentures, dental implants allow you to fully taste your food, and chew on whatever you’re craving– provided you’re healed from surgery, of course. Your oral hygiene also stays the same after getting dental implants, because you can care for them like regular teeth. Implants are an excellent way to take care of your oral health while maintaining your current lifestyle. You can brush, floss, and eat with implants functioning just like your natural teeth. Dental implants may have a higher initial cost, but they keep your diet and care consistent.


## Dental Implants Can Look Like Natural Teeth


Worrying over the look and feel of your new dental implants is normal. For the life-changing benefits that implants can offer, it’s worth moving past these concerns. Remember that modern implants are customizable and skilled dentistry can match your existing teeth. Any teeth you’re currently missing may also impact your pronunciation, and implants can provide a foundation for clear speech. So not only can implants look great, they can help you sound great too. Your confidence may even benefit from dental implants!


## Dental Implants May Last A Lifetime


Dental implants are known as a more expensive option, but they’re also the longer-lasting one. While alternatives like dentures will provide a less expensive fix initially, they require more frequent maintenance. Dentures require regular refitting, but implants can last a lifetime with proper dental care. This means the upfront cost can have a huge benefit to your long term oral health.


## Dental Implant Rejection is Rare


Many hopeful patients have worries for the implant process, particularly that their body will reject their dental implants. In reality, dental implants have a 95% success rate. This is because dental implants act like your real teeth. Dental implants are installed with titanium, a material the body naturally accepts. Patients with complications generally have other competing medical conditions. You can check with your dentist about potential complications connected to your medical history, but remember that these complications are rare. With modern technology, precise planning is possible, upping your likelihood of success. Worries are normal for any procedure, but don’t let dental anxiety stop you from finding the best solutions for you.


## Getting Dental Implants can Aid Oral Health and Prevent Bone Loss


Intervention from dental implants can also prevent further bone loss in your mouth and jaw. Missing teeth can lead to bone deterioration and can cause a “sunken face” appearance over time. Dental implants can stimulate your jawbone just like your other teeth, preventing that deterioration. They also protect healthy neighboring teeth and maintain proper spacing and bite.


## So, Will You Choose Dental Implants?


Not everyone is a candidate for dental implants. If you’re curious about what implants can offer, ask your dentist if you may qualify for them. Check in about what your dental insurance covers for dental implant procedures. When talking with your dentist, don’t be afraid to express potential concerns about the success of dental implants. Your dentist has likely walked patients through the same thing many times!

If you’re looking for implant dentistry in the Los Angeles area, look into Wilshire Oral Surgery. Wilshire offers a clear explanation of dental implant costs and other options for replacing missing teeth. Wilshire’s dental implant experts can reassure you of any concerns and help you take good care of your teeth and gums.

# Care for Your Dental Implants With Wilshire Oral Surgery


So you got new dental implants! With a little attention to your dental health, implants can last a lifetime. Dental implants are a popular solution for replacing missing teeth, and for good reason. They can last a lifetime with proper care, and can be easier to upkeep than dentures. In this article, we'll review caring for your implants immediately after surgery, avoiding dental implant failure, and simple care and maintenance.


## After Dental Implant Surgery – Care Instructions


Proper care is essential in the days after surgery. Immediately after your surgery, there are some simple dos and don’ts for your implants to heal properly:


### Don’t:


Smoke or use straws for the first 48 hours after surgery.

Reach for hard, crunchy foods.

Eat very hot foods initially.

Reach for any hard foods that could get trapped near the implant, like popcorn or seeds.

Drink alcoholic beverages that may irritate the implant.

Sleep on your side.

Brush the implant area.

Engage in intense physical activity.


### Do:


Keep the surgical issue clean with antiseptic mouthwash if instructed.

Rinse your mouth with salt water 2-3 times a day.

Ice the area for the first 24 hours.

Bite on a gauze pad for 20 or 30 minutes to help with minor bleeding.

Take prescribed pain medication and anti-inflammatories to mitigate pain.

Stick to soft foods like mashed potatoes, smoothies, or ice cream.


## What To Expect: Implant Care After Surgery


Over several months, the metal post that holds your implant in place will undergo osseointegration. This is the process during which your jawbone joins with your implant, allowing it to fully integrate with your mouth. Unless you need a second surgery to place your abutment, this isn’t something you need to be concerned with – it’s just helpful to know that your implant will be solidly attached. Patients choosing dental implants in Santa Monica and West LA will go through this same integration process.

Once approved by your dentist, you can gently brush to clean near the implants and surrounding gums. Avoid brushing too harshly and use a soft-bristled toothbrush. For single implants, be sure to floss daily to support the health of your surrounding teeth and help prevent gum disease. You can even consider getting a water flosser to really up your dental hygiene!

Compared to traditional dentures, dental implants don’t require as much upkeep from your dental hygienist, but maintenance and care at home is still vital.


## Preventing Implant Failure and Complications


It’s natural to worry about implant failure, but remember that with proper maintenance, your implants will be completely fine.

Here are some concerns you may want to watch for with dental implants:

Infection, injury, or damage near the implant

Nerve damage

Implant failure

Implant failure is a common concern but an uncommon occurrence. If you’re experiencing regular pain or gum recession around your implant, your implant feels loose, or you’re unable to chew comfortably, those can all be signs of implant failure. Smoking, grinding your teeth, and underlying medical conditions can lead to implant failure. However, if you take careful care of your overall oral health, it’s very likely your implants will be successful.


## Implant Care Long Term – Make Your Implants Last!


With proper at-home care and regular dental checkups, dental implants can last a lifetime. If you’re looking for competent oral surgeons in the Los Angeles area, check out Wilshire Oral Surgery. Our dental team can give additional care tips to help reduce pain and swelling during the healing process. When you work with a strong surgical team and maintain proper care and maintenance, it’s possible to keep your implants healthy and make them last a lifetime.

# What Is The Recovery Time for Zygomatic Implants? What to Expect During Your Full-Mouth Reconstruction Journey


When it comes to full-mouth reconstruction, zygomatic implants offer a revolutionary solution for patients with severe bone loss in the upper jaw. Unlike traditional dental implants that require significant bone grafting, zygomatic implants anchor into the strong zygomatic (cheek) bone, providing immediate stability and allowing for a faster overall treatment timeline. If you are considering zygomatic implants as part of your full-mouth reconstruction, understanding the recovery process is essential.


## What to Expect After Surgery


Zygomatic implant surgery is a complex procedure that requires specialized expertise. It is typically performed under general anesthesia or IV sedation, ensuring patient comfort throughout the process. Immediately following surgery, you can expect:

Mild to Moderate Swelling: Swelling is common in the first few days and usually peaks around 48 hours post-surgery before gradually subsiding.

Discomfort and Soreness: Some discomfort is expected, but it is manageable with prescribed or over-the-counter pain medication.

Minor Bruising: Due to the involvement of the cheekbone, slight bruising in the cheek area may occur but should fade within a week or two.

Soft Diet: Patients will need to follow a soft-food diet for the first few weeks to avoid unnecessary pressure on the implants.


### Recovery Timeline


The recovery time for zygomatic implants is often shorter than traditional implant procedures, primarily because bone grafting is not required. For patients who qualify for conventional dental implants in Los Angeles, the recovery process follows a slightly different path that includes a dedicated osseointegration phase. While individual healing rates vary, here is a general timeline of what you can expect:

First Week: The initial healing phase involves managing swelling, discomfort, and any minor bleeding. Sticking to soft foods and avoiding strenuous activity will aid recovery.

Two to Three Weeks: Most patients can resume normal daily activities, though heavy lifting and intense physical exertion should still be avoided. Swelling and bruising should be significantly reduced by this stage.

One to Two Months: Soft tissues around the implants should be fully healed, and patients typically receive their final prosthetic teeth within a few months after initial placement.

Three to Six Months: Full osseointegration (the process of the implants fusing with the bone) is expected to be complete. Patients can return to a normal diet, including harder foods, and enjoy full function and aesthetics.


### Long-Term Success and Care


After your full-mouth reconstruction with zygomatic implants, proper oral hygiene and regular follow-ups with your oral surgeon and dentist are crucial. Routine check-ups will help ensure the long-term stability and health of your implants. Maintaining good oral hygiene habits, such as brushing, flossing, and using an antibacterial mouth rinse, will also contribute to their longevity.


### Schedule a Consultation Today


Zygomatic implants provide an innovative and effective solution for patients with severe upper jaw bone loss, reducing the need for bone grafting and significantly improving the recovery timeline. While healing varies from patient to patient, most individuals can expect to resume their normal routines within a few weeks and achieve full integration within a few months.

If you are considering full-mouth reconstruction or want to learn more about zygomatic implants, contact Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center to schedule a consultation. Visit our office in Los Angeles, California, or call (310) 954-9449 to book an appointment today.

# The All-on-4 Dental Procedure: Step-by-Step Process Explained


Losing teeth can affect your daily life. It makes you feel shy about smiling. Simple tasks like eating become difficult ordeals. Yet, those old-fashioned dentures do not cut it. They lack stability and security. However, there is an excellent permanent solution called dental implants. It is revolutionary. The All-on-4 procedure allows doctors to replace your entire upper or lower set of teeth. Four implants are all it takes to anchor an entire arch of beautiful new teeth. This technique restores stunning, natural smiles that function well. You can grin with pride and eat whatever you want again. Imagine how that would transform your life. This dental implant procedure makes it possible.


## About All-on-4


The All-on-4 was a game-changer for dental implants. It made replacing an entire arch of teeth a breeze. Only four implants are needed for maximum support. For patients replacing individual missing teeth, dental implants in West Los Angeles remain the most precise and lasting solution. With less hardware in your mouth, you achieve the desired result—a permanent new set of teeth.

Fewer implants mean faster healing, too. The All-on-4 was a solution that made implants accessible to more people. It upgraded and simplified the whole process.


### Missing Teeth’s Detrimental Effects


Living with missing teeth takes a heavy toll. Embarrassment and low self-confidence plague your daily life. You hesitate about simple joys like laughing. Eating favorite foods becomes difficult or impossible. Traditional dentures help but have drawbacks. Slippage and irritation often occur while eating or speaking.


### Benefits of the Procedure


These dental implants offer unmatched stability and comfort. The innovative angled implant placement maximizes support. Replacing an entire arch allows confident smiling and eating again. Food tastes and feels more appealing when chewed. Self-esteem soars from a beautiful new smile.


### The Step-by-Step Process


Consultation and Planning

The first step is a consultation appointment. Experienced implant dentists examine the mouth. They take X-rays and discuss goals with patients. This visit identifies any preparatory treatments needed. Sample teeth help you visualize your future smile during planning.

Preparatory Treatments

Some preliminary steps occur before implant surgery. The dentist extracts the remaining teeth during the same surgery visit. Bone grafting procedures may build up thin jawbone areas. Temporary dentures are created to wear post-surgery.

Implant Placement Surgery

Surgery day is the most significant step of the process. Dentists numb the mouth completely for patient comfort. They place four implant posts into the jawbone. Two straight anterior implants stabilize the front and the other two posterior implants angle for maximized back support.

Healing and Osseointegration

Jawbone healing around the implants is the crucial next step. This osseointegration process fuses implant and bone over several months. Patients wear temporary dentures during this integrating stage. Soft foods comprise the recommended diet following treatment.

Attaching the Final Prosthesis

When bones heal, the transformation culminates. Dentists secure a permanent full-arch prosthesis onto the four implants. This new set of replacement teeth looks natural, yet it remains fixed in place.


### Benefits of All-on-4 Vs. Traditional Dentures


Conventional dentures rest on gums without anchors. All-on-4 upgrades every aspect compared to this approach. Implants integrate into bone like natural tooth roots would. Secured teeth feel stable while chewing all foods—no more denture cream mess or nightly removal needed.


### Recovery Experience


The procedure may result in some minor swelling and discomfort. Pain medication manages any temporary surgical symptoms well. Patients transition to a lifelong diet without restrictions. Within weeks, the new set of teeth feels like a natural part of the mouth.


### Meticulous Oral Hygiene Needed


Caring for your implants ensures lasting success. Excellent brushing and flossing habits must continue daily. Routine dental cleanings remove hardened plaque buildup. Taking these maintenance steps prevents gum disease or implant failure in the long term.

This dental technique creates life-changing improvements. Restored bite strength boosts nutrition from unrestricted eating. Speaking clarity increases without slippage. Also, beautiful teeth revitalize self-confidence and social lives. The investment provides priceless returns for years.

For more on the All-on-4 Dental Procedure, visit Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center at our office in Los Angeles, California. Call (310) 954-9449 to schedule an appointment today.

# Sinus Lift Surgery: Learn About Enhancing Your Smile and Boosting Bone Structure


A healthy, confident smile often begins with strong, stable bone structure in the jaw. Unfortunately, bone loss in the upper jaw can pose challenges for patients seeking dental implants. For individuals with insufficient bone density, sinus lift surgery offers a solution, paving the way for effective implant placement while enhancing oral health and aesthetics.


## What Is a Sinus Lift?


A sinus lift, also known as sinus augmentation, is a surgical procedure designed to increase bone height in the upper jaw by adding bone material to the area near the molars and premolars. The procedure involves lifting the sinus membrane to create space for the new bone material, which integrates with the existing bone over time.

This surgery is often recommended for patients who have experienced bone loss due to factors such as:

Tooth Loss: Missing teeth in the upper jaw for an extended period can lead to bone resorption.

Periodontal Disease: Advanced gum disease can weaken the jawbone.

Anatomy of the Sinus Cavity: Naturally large sinus cavities can limit available bone for implant placement.


### The Sinus Lift Procedure


The sinus lift procedure is performed under local anesthesia, with or without sedation, depending on the patient’s comfort level. During the surgery:

Incision and Access: A small incision is made in the gum tissue to expose the jawbone.

Sinus Membrane Elevation: The sinus membrane is gently lifted away from the bone.

Bone Grafting: Bone material, either from the patient or a biocompatible source, is placed into the newly created space.

Healing Period: The grafted bone integrates with the existing jawbone over a healing period, which can take several months.


### Benefits of Sinus Lift Surgery


Sinus lift surgery plays a crucial role for many patients who are seeking dental implants, especially when bone loss in the upper jaw is a concern. One of the primary benefits of this procedure is enhanced bone support. By adding bone material to the jaw, the surgery strengthens the area and creates a stable foundation for the secure placement of dental implants, ensuring long-term functionality and success.

In addition to improving the structural integrity of the jaw, sinus lift surgery also offers significant aesthetic benefits. Rebuilding bone structure can restore facial symmetry, addressing any changes in appearance caused by bone loss. For patients who have experienced hollowed or sunken cheeks, this procedure can enhance their overall facial profile, contributing to a more youthful and balanced look.

Lastly, sinus lift surgery supports long-term oral health by facilitating the placement of dental implants. Implants help reduce the risk of further bone loss by maintaining the jawbone’s integrity, unlike traditional dentures that can exacerbate resorption. Additionally, implants supported by a successful sinus lift help preserve the surrounding natural teeth, reducing the likelihood of shifting or further dental complications. This combination of structural, aesthetic, and health benefits makes sinus lift surgery an essential step for patients with upper jaw bone loss.


### Rebuild Your Smile with Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center


Sinus lift surgery offers a transformative solution for individuals with bone loss in the upper jaw. By enhancing bone structure, this procedure makes dental implants possible, restoring not only your smile but also your confidence and oral health. Whether you’re looking to replace missing teeth or prevent future bone loss, a sinus lift can help you achieve lasting results.

Contact Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center to schedule your consultation to determine if sinus lift surgery is right for you. Visit our office in Los Angeles, California, or call (310) 954-9449 to book an appointment today.

# Benefits of Dental Cone Beam CT: Cone Beam Computed Tomography & Imaging in Los Angeles


3D imaging is a relatively new dentistry practice. In years past, diagnostic processes used medical grade CTs or "CAT" scans to create clear imaging. 3D imaging allows dentists to plan for dental treatments like orthodontics or dental implants. Here, we'll dig into what dental cone beam computed tomography imaging (or CBCT) provides, and how treatment planning can benefit from it.


### What is Cone Beam Computed Tomography?


CBCT uses a “cone-shaped” X-ray, instead of a “fan-shaped” beam. This allows oral and maxillofacial structures to be captured in two dimensions. With a cone-shaped beam, diagnostic information can be found faster and at a lower radiation dose. This way, more complex diagnostic and treatment planning can be completed in a single scan.


### Why is Cone Beam CT different from Traditional X-Rays?


Cone Beam CT is easier and more cost-effective than a conventional “CT” scan or X-RAY. It allows your dentist to produce high-quality three dimensional images of the teeth and jaw. Compared to CT scans, cone beam imaging provides better visualization, more accurate scans, and lower levels of radiation. It’s an increasingly popular choice compared to traditional X-rays, as it can create a better process for the patient and surgeon.


### Dental Care Using CBCT


CBCT scanners are also more accessible to dental offices. They are less expensive, smaller, lighter, and offer better spatial resolution overall. Having a 3D view allows dentists to see anatomical structures, produce high-quality images from different angles, and create detailed surgical treatment plans.

Here are just some of the potential dental applications for CBCT three-dimensional imaging:

Assessment of bone volume for implant placement

Preparing for surgery to address impacted teeth

Planning for more than one complex implant surgery virtually

Discovering airway analysis for sleep apnea

Planning for bone reconstruction or grafting

Measuring proximity to important structures like the sinus and nerve pathways

Measuring the size of growths, tumors, or cysts in the jaws.

Planning jaw surgery virtually

Diagnosing TMJ

Locating impacted teeth in relationship to the skeleton

Diagnosing facial fractures and performing facial reconstruction.

Cone beam CT provides clearer, more detailed images than regular dental X-rays, and can improve care across a wide range of procedures.


### Do I need to prepare for a CBCT scan?


Heavy preparation shouldn’t be necessary for cone-beam computed tomography. You may need to remove items that will interfere with imaging, such as jewelry, hearing aids, or removable dental work. It’s also important to inform your surgeon if there is a possibility that you may be pregnant. Some scans are taken with the patient lying down, others are taken seated. A CBCT scan only takes 5 to 40 seconds. All patients need to do during the procedure is bite down in a specific jaw position, and then sit as still as possible. During the procedure, the scanner will rotate around the patient’s head to take images that will be combined into a 3-D image. During the scan, 150 to 200 images will be taken. The procedure is completely painless and noninvasive. After the procedure, patients can go about their day as normal. Your oral surgeon will analyze the images and contact you with the results and next steps.


### Nervous about CBCT Radiation Levels?


Are you concerned about radiation exposure with CBCT imaging? Cone beam CT actually provides significantly less radiation exposure than traditional dental X-rays. CBCT can be a very low-dose modality compared to traditional medical imaging. Dosages are also progressively decreasing. CBCT technology allows for an accurate diagnosis with a relatively low dose of radiation. An upper or lower jaw scan to prepare for and diagnose dental issues is about 95 µSv. Comparatively, a coast-to-coast round-trip flight is 30 µSv, so if you travel frequently, this isn’t a big difference! Traditional CT scanners are much higher in radiation. A regular mammogram is over 4 times the µSv of a CBCT jaw scan. A CT of your abdomen or pelvis clocks in at 10,000 µSv. It’s understandable to be concerned about radiation with CT scans, but remember that this one is relatively minor. Remember that your dentist is as concerned with your health as you are.


### 3D Cone Beam Imaging at Wilshire Oral Surgery


If you’re looking for state-of-the-art technology and a smooth dental experience in Los Angeles, check out Wilshire Oral Surgery. Wilshire’s oral surgeons truly care about patient outcomes and are committed to providing quality care. CBCT imaging technology is commonly used at Wilshire, and our surgeons are committed to providing a positive and safe experience. Choose a dental office that provides more with Wilshire.
